full_text: After Apple wrapped up its “Surprise and shine” event today, we were able to get a look at the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Hands-on with the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 Apple’s latest watches come with some new Siri AI features and the return of ceramic cases. Apple’s latest watches come with some new Siri AI features and the return of ceramic cases. Both of the new watches launch September 18th, with preorders available starting today. The Apple Watch Series 12 once again starts at $399 for the aluminum case option in space gray, black, light gold, and dark bronze aluminum. The natural or radiant gold titanium version costs $699, and the night blue or pearl white ceramic costs $899. Apple says this year’s watch offers up to 24 hours of “everyday” battery life, and now offers up to 10 hours of battery during outdoor workouts and supports faster charging with up to 12 hours’ worth recharged in just 15 minutes. The ceramic Series 12 sure does look and feel nice in person. The night blue version is very fetching, but the stark pearl white is also très chic on the wrist. The new dark bronze did look a lot darker in person, however. Like how the dark green Series 7 looked a bit less green and more blackish green, there’s a similar vibe with the bronze. The Series 12 runs on a new S11 chip that powers a few new Audio Intelligence Siri AI features, including Sound Recognition, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It also got some health upgrades, including new optical and electrical heart sensors with support for continuous background heart rate sensing that takes readings every five seconds. There’s also a new Health Age feature that compares your health metrics to your chronological age, and a Readiness feature that gives you a score for how to handle the day ahead based on your recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score. The Readiness feature will be limited to the Series 12 and Ultra 4, however, because it requires the new heart rate sensor array. Speaking of the array, this is the first major update on this front in a while. You can definitely see the difference side by side. Notably, the Apple reps on hand pointed out that the new Series 12 and Ultra 4 have a “32-petal design,” whereas the older watches had a two-petal design. This refers to the spoke-like lines coming out of the electrode. It should theoretically enable much more accurate readings. You can also see that the optical sensors themselves are situated much closer together. This is to help minimize light leakage. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 also includes the new S11 chip and Audio Intelligence features. It starts at $799 and comes in natural and black titanium, along with a premium Apple Watch Hermès version. Apple says the Ultra 4 offers up to 50 hours of battery life.

title_en: Researchers discuss how data center construction could influence voters and impact public land
summary: دیتاسنترهای غول‌پیکر هوش مصنوعی مصرف برق بی‌سابقه‌ای دارند؛ برخی معادل یک شهر ۸۰ هزار خانه‌ای انرژی مصرف می‌کنند.

full_text: Researchers discuss how data center construction could influence voters and impact public land The construction of new data centers is shaping up to be a defining issue in the 2026 midterm elections. Politicians in both parties have been distancing themselves from data centers in the face of public discontent around the issue, with public backlash leading to the freezing of dozens of data center projects nationwide this year. Recently, government officials have considered multiple new ways to construct data centers, including building data centers on federal lands and trading parkland with developers for data center construction. In this Q&A, Hannah Wiseman, a professor at Penn State Dickinson Law and the College of Earth and Mineral Sciences who specializes in land use regulation and energy law; and Derrick Taff, the Suzie and Allen Martin Professor of Recreation, Park, and Tourism Management and a former park ranger who studies the relationship between humans and wilderness areas, discuss potential issues associated with building data centers on federal land. Q: Will data centers be a factor when people vote this fall? Wiseman: Data centers are a bipartisan issue, in part because many of them are now being constructed in areas that have not experienced this type of development before. The Pew Research Center has an interesting study showing that the majority of data centers are emerging in rural areas, and many of them are in counties that have no existing data center infrastructure. The "hyperscale" data center is a relatively new form of development. A data center is essentially a very large warehouse, but unlike many warehouses, it uses a lot of water and energy. Hyperscale data centers are huge, with some occupying several thousand acres of land. Most people do things every day that require conventional data centers, such as streaming movies. But hyperscale data centers use approximately 100 megawatts of electricity or more, though definitions vary. One of these centers uses the same amount of electricity daily that a medium- or large-sized city—around 80,000 houses or even 800,000 homes—would use daily. Hyperscale data centers primarily power technologies that are different from our typical daily use, like complex artificial intelligence (AI) models. Although these data centers are necessary infrastructure for AI, not all individuals use AI for complex tasks on a daily basis. Many of these AI models are designed for very sophisticated business uses, so some communities are asking, "Hey, wait a minute, do we really need this hyperscale AI data center?" Residents are starting to see how this could change their communities. They are speaking with their state leaders, which is why we're seeing a pause on all new data centers in states like Texas and a new executive order from Gov. Josh Shapiro in Pennsylvania placing more requirements on data center construction. Q: Can you explain the executive order that was intended to facilitate data center development? Wiseman: In 2025, the federal government issued an executive order titled, "Accelerating Federal Permitting of Data Center Infrastructure." It directs federal agencies to use federally owned land and resources for the expeditious and orderly development of data centers. There is now one approved data center on public lands managed by the Bureau of Land Management, although construction is currently paused. Recently, the federal government has also encouraged data center construction on federal lands that are already polluted. These are not necessarily recreation areas, but former military sites—areas previously used for the development and testing of weapons. Q: Are there specific concerns about data centers on federal lands? Wiseman: A data center on federal lands that are not polluted would contradict what many residents in the United States think of as the purpose of federally protected land—for wilderness purposes, recreation and the preservation of cultural and aesthetic resources. These are similar to concerns surrounding mining or oil and gas development. Many of these lands are supposed to have multiple uses. There are congressional directives about how these lands should be available for all Americans and used for a variety of purposes. Some of those purposes are for economic development. Some federal lands can be used for livestock grazing, and many are used for oil and gas development or mining. For many residents, a data center seems to push that logic too far. It's simply not using the natural resources on the land. The facilities constructed would be relatively permanent, resource-intensive infrastructure. Q: What would be the impact of building data centers in national forests? Taff: National forests are administered by the Department of Agriculture and are under different mandates than our national parks. Regulations in these forests allow for recreation, but also the extraction of natural resources. However, national forests are often located adjacent to our national parks; if data centers are built on national forest land, that very well could affect any adjacent national park as well. Even though we have boundaries to parks and forests on paper, wildlife doesn't recognize these distinctions, and human-caused light and noise pollution travel beyond those boundaries. Data centers are going to require a lot of infrastructure and a lot of energy. As a society and as scientists, we're not sure how data centers would affect the surrounding communities or the ecological health of national parks or forests. It's something that we need to be very mindful of, and I think there needs to be a lot more research before things move too quickly. Q: What risks does development pose to wild animals and humans? Taff: I'll use the impact of light as an example. Over the last century, humans have rapidly decreased our ability to see the natural night sky, as sky glow from lighting is increasing at a rate of approximately 10% each yea

full_text: Apple today introduced its first foldable device, named the iPhone Duo, at its Surprise and Shine event held in Cupertino. The phone is the first marquee device launched under the company’s new CEO, John Ternus. Unlike early iterations of foldables, which looked like vertical slabs, Apple adopted a wider form factor that could aid in a better aspect ratio while watching videos when the device is unfolded. The unfolded display is a 7.6-inch Retina display, and the outer display is 5.4 inches. The company said that the new device was “inspired by the versatility of iPad” and showed how people can use it unfolded in a vertical mode. The inner display also features an “under-display” camera that can give users an all-screen feel. Apple said that it used a custom nanotexture finish to hide the crease and reduce glare. Most foldables still have a visible crease, but companies like Oppo have made strides toward an almost seamless phone. The company claimed that its hinge was created using grade 5 aluminum and over 100 special components for smooth opening and closing and durability. Notably, the device only has Touch ID, with Face ID missing. You can unlock the device using the Apple Watch, though. The device is powered by the new A20 Pro chip and C2 model, which allows for faster uploads. Just like last year’s iPhone Air, this particular model is eSIM-only. On the battery front, the company said that with the inner display, users can get 31 hours of video playback, and with the outer display, 44 hours of video playback. The phone features a 48-megapixel fusion main camera and a 48-megapixel ultrawide camera with 2x optical zoom. This dual-camera setup skips a telephoto camera. Just like other foldables, users can take rear-camera selfies and look at previews on the outer display. It also has a Google Pixel-like feature that plays an animation on the outer display, which is useful when you are trying to get kids to focus while taking photos. There is also a smart-take feature that uses an on-device model and snaps an image when all subjects within the frame are posing. The company has made iOS 27 adaptable to the new foldable — essential controls like Wi-Fi move to the side and dock on the home screen vertically oriented. Users can use apps in split screen and also pair the apps. If someone is using the phone vertically, they can pin a video on top and use other apps in the bottom half. One of the fascinating features is that users will be able to use the iPhone half folded or even set it on a table. Apple noted that later this year, the device will support Apple Pencil. The iPhone Duo is priced at $1,999 with 256GB storage and comes in two colors. Preorders for Apple’s new foldable begin on October 16, and the device will be available on October 23. Rivals like Samsung and Xiaomi have already launched their version of wide foldables before Apple. According to analytics firm Counterpoint, foldables contribute to less than 2% of shipments in the overall smartphone market. However, Apple’s new phone could be an instant hit, as the analytics firm said the Duo could garner up to 25% market share by the end of the year.

full_text: Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max at its event on Wednesday. The 18 Pro and Pro Max come in deep black, silver, “glacier,” and burgundy, with color-matched back glass. They also have a new A20 Pro chip and purportedly the longest battery in an iPhone. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 for 256GB, a $100 increase over the iPhone 17 Pro, while the 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299, also for 256GB. Both models will be offered in 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, and 2TB configurations. Preorders begin on September 12th ahead of availability on September 18th. Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro has a dynamic aperture main camera The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max have powerful new camera features. The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max have powerful new camera features. During Wednesday’s presentation, Apple highlighted how the new phones are well-equipped to work with Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, including Siri AI’s more expressive voices. The A20 Pro has a “brand new architecture” built on 2nm technology, like Apple’s M6 chip. It has a 6-core CPU with two “desktop-class” super cores and four efficiency cores. It also has a “significantly advanced” GPU with a 7-core design that enables a “40 percent” increase in performance, according to Sribalan Santhanam, VP of Apple’s silicon engineering group. Apple has also added a second neural engine for a total of 32 NPU cores. In addition, the iPhone 18 Pro has a “next-generation vapor chamber” with three times the surface area as the one in the 17 Pro to help cool the phone. The iPhone 18 Pro has all-day battery life comparable to the iPhone 17 Pro Max, according to Rich Dinh, VP of hardware engineering. Video playback is 36 hours for the iPhone 18 Pro, and the 18 Pro Max gets 45 hours. Apple says just 15 minutes of wired charging provides 50 percent charge for the iPhone 18 Pro, and for the 18 Pro Max, five minutes of wired charging gets you seven hours of video playback. The iPhone 18 Pro also offers the “biggest camera improvement in years,” including a 48 megapixel variable-aperture main camera with six blades “thinner than a human hair” and a new sensor. In darker environments, the aperture opens up to let in more light, which means that night mode captures will be faster with better quality, Apple says. As for video, you can now take 4K resolution time-lapse videos in Dolby Vision HDR. Apple is also offering “Pro controls” to give you more manual control over your camera, like changing shutter speed to tweak motion blur. Pro controls are available for both photos and videos. There are improvements to photographic styles, offering texture and grain control. And Apple will support Google’s SynthID content authenticity protocol, as well as a new “Apple Reference Image” standard that cryptographically signs images at capture, creating an unalterable “digital negative.” A smaller Dynamic Island on the iPhone 18 Pro line can now show three Live Activities. There are updated accessories as well, including a revised clear case. The iPhone 18 Pro line is also Apple’s first set of phones with a new C2 cellular modem, which supports mmWave 5G and “delivers meaningfully faster uploads when compared to C1X while consuming 15 percent less energy,” Apple says. The new phones follow a major redesign introduced with the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max in 2025. That redesign dropped titanium in favor of an aluminum body, introduced a vapor chamber to help keep the phone cool, and added a camera bar (which Apple calls the “plateau”) that stretches across the back. The 17 Pro line also launched in a bold orange color that was good and well-timed, a nice silver, and a great deep blue. And last fall’s iPhone refresh brought the 18-megapixel Center Stage front camera that lets you take wide selfies even when you’re holding the phone in portrait mode.

title_fa: دستاورد جدید OpenAI در حل مساله‌ای ریاضی با قدمت یک قرن
title_en: OpenAI says AI solved one of math's hardest problems in days
summary: مدل جدید و منتشرنشده OpenAI موفق شد طی چند روز و با به‌کارگیری ۱۰ هزار ایجنت همزمان، مسئله سخت ناوویه-استوکس را حل کند.
این مسئله که جزو مسائل هزاره ریاضیات است، فرمول‌بندی پیش‌بینی هوا، طراحی هواپیما و جریان خون را دگرگون می‌کند.

full_text: OpenAI said Tuesday that one of its unreleased artificial intelligence models had solved a mathematical puzzle that has eluded mathematicians for generations, in a claim which also drew a fight with rival researchers over credit. Researchers at OpenAI said it took just days -- and millions of dollars in computing power -- to crack what is known as the Navier-Stokes problem. Navier-Stokes is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, a list of the hardest open questions in mathematics drawn up by the Clay Mathematics Institute. It concerns the equations describing how fluids such as air and water move, which are used in aircraft design, weather forecasting and the study of blood flow. OpenAI said its work showed that these equations can break down over time, answering the question as set out by the Millennium Prize. "This is a significant milestone for AI research, and its promise for the world is that even more of our hardest questions would become possible to answer," Mark Chen, OpenAI's chief research officer, told reporters. Each Millennium Prize Problem carries a $1 million reward, and only one has been solved since the list was published in 2000. OpenAI says it will not claim money if its finding is confirmed. According to the prize rules, a solution has to be published in a peer-reviewed journal and survive two years after gaining acceptance in the mathematical community before the institute will even convene a committee to consider the work. "The process of evaluation is deliberately unhurried, and we shall ensure that it is absolutely rigorous," Professor Martin Bridson, President of the Clay Mathematics Institute, told AFP. ChatGPT-style AI is revolutionizing the world of high-level math by quickly solving famous, long-unsolved problems that stumped experts for decades. But it has also sparked debate over whether machine-generated answers truly count as real human understanding. - 'Millions of dollars' - In a blog post describing the breakthrough, OpenAI said it began training a new model in late August, more capable than anything it had released publicly. Days later, seeing online rumors that a competitor had solved Millennium problems, OpenAI turned the system loose on all six that remain open. Work on Navier-Stokes showed unexpected promise, and the company poured its computing power into it. By the final stage, OpenAI researcher Sebastien Bubeck said, 10,000 AI agents -- programs that operate on their own -- were working on the problem at once, passing messages back and forth. Chen said the computing costs ran "emphatically in the millions of dollars," with Bubeck adding this was roughly 1,000 times what the company spent on earlier mathematical results. According to OpenAI's account, the agents reached a solution Saturday, about 88 hours after launching the project. The claim arrived hours after Tristan Buckmaster, a mathematician at New York University, and Levent Alpoge, who works at OpenAI competitor Anthropic, released their own AI-assisted work on three related equations. In a statement published alongside his papers, Buckmaster said OpenAI had taken up the problem only after word of his research spread, and pursued the same unusual approach he and Alpoge had spent months developing. OpenAI's researchers denied having had any access to the rival team's work and said they proposed sharing credit before realizing that Buckmaster and Alpoge had fallen short of solving the problem. "To be clear, we did not use their prompts or proofs to prompt our models or direct our agents," Bubeck said. However, in a later post on X, OpenAI said "while unlikely, we cannot rule out that de-identified data derived from their usage of our products helped improve our models." arp-tu/md

title_fa: استعفای محقق آنتروپیک در اعتراض به مسابقه خطرناک هوش مصنوعی
title_en: واهمه از هوش مصنوعی خارج از کنترل، پژوهشگر آنتروپیک را ناچار به استعفا کرد
summary: جیکوب کاکسون، پژوهشگر برجسته آنتروپیک، به دلیل نگرانی از ساخت مدل‌های هوش مصنوعی خودبهبوددهنده و خارج از کنترل انسانی از این شرکت استعفا داد.
او معتقد است رقابت فشرده میان شرکت‌های آمریکایی و چینی باعث نادیده‌گرفتن استانداردهای ایمنی برای عقب نماندن از بازار شده است.
به باور این محقق، بدون مداخله دولت‌ها یا کند شدن هماهنگ توسعه در کل صنعت، ساخت مسئولانه هوش مصنوعی عمومی (AGI) ناممکن خواهد بود.
full_text: بهنوشته والاستریت ژورنال جیکوب کاکسون، یکی از پژوهشگران آنتروپیک بهدلیل نگرانی از اینکه این آزمایشگاه و رقبایش برای ساخت سیستمهایی از هوش مصنوعی با یکدیگر در رقابتی هستند که ممکن است قادر به کنترل آنها نباشند، صنعت هوش مصنوعی را ترک میکند؛ اقدامی که نشانهای از افزایش نگرانیهای ایمنی در درون شرکتهای پیشرو هوش مصنوعی است. جیکوب کاکسون در زمینه آموزش مدلهای جدید هوش مصنوعی از طریق تغذیه آنها با حجم عظیمی از دادهها تخصص دارد. او سهشنبه ۱۷ شهریور گفت شرکت را ترک میکند، زیرا نمیخواهد در رقابت گسترده صنعت برای ساخت سیستمهای هوش مصنوعی مشارکت داشته باشد که قادرند خودشان را بهبود دهند. او نگران است چنین سیستمهایی از کنترل خارج شوند و بشریت را نابود کنند. این بریتانیایی ۲۷ ساله که پیشتر ریاضیات خوانده، به والاستریت ژورنال گفت بسیاری از همکارانش در این صنعت اکنون برای توصیف مسیر حرکت به سوی مدلهای خودبهبوددهنده از عباراتی مانند «لحظه سرنوشتساز» (crunchtime) و «بازی نهایی» (endgame) استفاده میکنند. کاکسون گفت: «ما در مسیری قرار داریم که به بسیاری از تهاجمیترین سناریوها منتهی میشود؛ سناریوهایی که بر اساس آنها ممکن است تا پایان سال آینده اوضاع از کنترل خارج شده باشد.» او افزود زمانی که شرکتها با یکدیگر و همچنین با شرکتهای نوظهور چینی رقابت میکنند، مصالحه و کوتاه آمدن در زمینه ایمنی اجتنابناپذیر است. آنتروپیک بلافاصله درباره این جدایی اظهار نظر نکرد. داریو آمودی، مدیرعامل آنتروپیک، و دیگر مدیران این شرکت بارها درباره خطرات مدلهای هوش مصنوعی سرکش هشدار داده و خواستهاند سرعت توسعه را کاهش دهد. کاکسون گفت او اوایل امسال اوپنایآی (OpenAI) را ترک کرد تا به آنتروپیک بپیوندد، زیرا این شرکت به تلاشهایش در زمینه ایمنی مدلها شهرت دارد. اما با وجود اینکه او تلاشهای آنتروپیک در زمینه ایمنی را جدی و صادقانه یافت، اکنون معتقد است در غیاب مداخله دولت یا کاهش هماهنگ سرعت توسعه در سراسر صنعت، هیچ شرکتی نمیتواند بهطور مسئولانه هوشی مصنوعی توسعه دهد که در طیف وسیعی از وظایف عملکردی بهتر از انسانها داشته باشد؛ چیزی که گاهی هوش مصنوعی عمومی (AGI) نامیده میشود. هکهای اخیر انجامشده از سوی مدلهای اوپنایآی و آنتروپیک، که برخی از آنها در قالب مجموعههایی از عاملهای هوش مصنوعی که با یکدیگر همکاری میکنند فعالیت داشتهاند، نشان دادهاند که چگونه سیستمهای هوش مصنوعی میتوانند اهداف مخرب را در پیش بگیرند و تلاش کنند این اهداف را از انسانها پنهان کنند. کاکسون گفت نگران است زمانی که این سیستمها شروع به بهبود دادن خودشان کنند، آنقدر پیشرفت کنند که بتوانند از اجرای دستورات سر باز بزنند. خروج کاکسون یکی از نخستین نمونههای استعفای یک کارمند آنتروپیک بهدلیل نگرانیهای مربوط به ایمنی هوش مصنوعی است. یک پژوهشگر حوزه ایمنی نیز اوایل امسال این شرکت را ترک کرد تا به مطالعه شعر بپردازد و هشدار داد که «جهان در معرض خطر است.» در سالهای اخیر و همچنین در گذشته، چندین پژوهشگر اوپنایآی و شرکتهای دیگر نیز با اشاره به نگرانیهای مشابه از سمتهای خود کنارهگیری کردهاند. آنتروپیک یکی از بزرگترین پلتفرمهای هوش مصنوعی را تا حدی با این ادعا ایجاد کرده است که توسعه مسئولانه هوش مصنوعی را در اولویت قرار میدهد و سرمایهگذاری سنگینی در این حوزه انجام داده است. رهبران این صنعت هشدار دادهاند که حملات سایبری اخیر میتواند نشانهای از آنچه در آینده رخ خواهد داد باشد. اوپنایآی هفته گذشته به خبرنگاران گفت جدیدترین مدل این شرکت مصداق هوش مصنوعی عمومی است و جهشی بزرگ در قابلیتها محسوب میشود. سم آلتمن، مدیرعامل اوپنایآی، هفته گذشته در نشستی در کارولینای شمالی به مقامهای گروه ۲۰ گفت: «فکر میکنم اگر مردم با فوریت بسیار زیادی اقدام نکنند، در حوزه امنیت سایبری اتفاقات بسیار بدی رخ خواهد داد.» یاکوب پاچوکی، دانشمند ارشد اوپنایآی، نیز در یادداشتی که روز یکشنبه در وبلاگ خود منتشر کرد و در آن خواستار کاهش هماهنگ سرعت توسعه در صنعت و مداخله دولت شد، نوشت:«اکنون زمانی است که احتیاط فوقالعادهای را میطلبد. من نگرانم که هیچکس برای پیامدهای ادامه افزایش سریع هوش ماشینی آماده نباشد.» کاکسون، پاچوکی و آمودی به بیش از هزار پژوهشگر هوش مصنوعی در سراسر این صنعت پیوستهاند که اخیرا بیانیهای را امضا کردند و در آن خواستار هماهنگی جهانی دولتها برای ایجاد سازوکاری شدهاند که اگر برای کنترل مدلهای قادر به بهبود دادن خودشان به یک «پدال ترمز» نیاز باشد، بتوان سرعت توسعه هوش مصنوعی را کاهش داد. در سطح فدرال آمریکا هیچ مقرراتی برای هوش مصنوعی وجود ندارد و دولت ترامپ رویکردی با حداقل مداخله را در اولویت قرار داده است تا منافع اقتصادی هوش مصنوعی را به حداکثر برساند؛ فضایی که منتقدان میگویند ممکن است به حملات سایبری گسترده یا آسیبهای دیگر منجر شود. سناتور برنی سندرز و گرگ کاسار، نماینده دموکرات تگزاس، دو تن از معدود قانونگذارانی هستند که پیشنهاد ایجاد محدودیتهای حفاظتی برای هوش مصنوعی را مطرح کردهاند. آنها هفته گذشته طرحی قانونی ارائه کردند که هدف آن ممنوعیت دائمی ابرهوش مصنوعی و توقف توسعه مدلها تا زمانی است که یک نهاد تنظیمگر صنعت، مقررات جدیدی وضع کند. خروج کاکسون از صنعت هوش مصنوعی در شرایطی صورت میگیرد که آنتروپیک خود را برای عرضه اولیه سهام آماده میکند؛ عرضهای که انتظار میرود یکی از بزرگترین عرضههای اولیه سهام در تاریخ باشد. این شرکت بهدنبال دستیابی به ارزشگذاری دو تریلیون دلاری است و در جریان جذب سرمایهگذاران، بر توسعه مسئولانه این فناوری تاکید کرده است. آمودی و دیگر مدیران شرکت گاه بر سر شیوههایی که بهگفته آنها ایمنی هوش مصنوعی را در اولویت قرار نمیدهند، با دولت ترامپ و دیگر مدیران صنعت وارد تقابل شدهاند. کاکسون گفت آنتروپیک از یک کانال داخلی در اسلک (Slack) کارکنان برای بحث درباره قابلیتهای قدرتمند مدلهای خود استفاده میکند. او این موضوع را بازتابی از میزان نفوذ شرکتهای هوش مصنوعی بر مسیر توسعه این صنعت توصیف کرد. کاکسون گفت: «این واقعا یک جورهایی دیوانهکننده است که چنین چیزی باید روی مکبوکهای چند مهندس ساکن سانفرانسیسکو اتفاق بیفتد، نه در یک پناهگاه در دل بیابان، مثل جایی که پروژه منهتن را انجام میدادند.»
impact: افزایش فشارهای نظارتی و بدبینی عمومی نسبت به رقابت بی‌رویه غول‌های AI در توسعه مدل‌های خودمختار.

title_fa: سرقت مخفیانه توکن‌های کلود؛ هکرها حساب کاربران آنتروپیک را خالی می‌کنند
title_en: Hackers are stealing Claude tokens from subscribers
summary: هکرها با سرقت کلیدهای جلسه (Session Keys) در کلود، از توکن‌های کاربران اشتراکی برای سرویس‌های ثالث استفاده می‌کنند.
عدم ارائه گزارش ریزمصرف توکن توسط آنتروپیک باعث شده کشف این سرقت‌ها ماه‌ها طول بکشد.
این رخنه امنیتی موجب مسدودی ناگهانی حساب‌های کاری و ضرر مالی به کسب‌وکارهای وابسته به هوش مصنوعی شده است.
full_text: On August 4, Grant De Swardt, an independent AI consultant in East Sussex, U.K., noticed something strange going on with his Claude Max 20x account. He hadn’t been working that day, yet his token usage was climbing. The next day, he disabled everything he had attached to Claude and did not work with it. Token consumption again increased. “In the clearest controlled interval, it increased from 45% to 55% while I performed no work, scheduled Cowork tasks were paused or completed, Dispatch/cloud execution was disabled, and there was no corresponding active local Claude Code task,” De Swardt told TechCrunch. What was eating up his token allowance? He had no idea, so he contacted Anthropic and asked for an itemized list. Anthropic didn’t provide one, but it agreed something was off. It suspended his paid account, invalidated all of his sessions and server-side Claude Code tokens, and issued him a partial refund of £44.49 for the remaining time on his $200-per-month subscription. The suspension wreaked havok on his business, he told TechCrunch. His job is to help small and mid-size businesses set up agents — a sort of forward-deployed engineer for hire — for tasks like automatically loading purchase-order data from emails into the accounting software. As a sole proprietor, he relies on agents throughout his whole business, too: daily admin tasks, website design, coding. “Like everything is just running through AI these days,” he said. After investigating, Anthropic told De Swardt it found the culprit: A compromised Claude session key was used to mint unauthorized Claude Code OAuth tokens. The company told him the account “appeared to have been used by an unauthorized-looking third-party service to handle activity for other people, but they could not determine how it obtained access,” he told TechCrunch. “They say the evidence is consistent either with credentials/session data being taken without my knowledge, or with the account having been connected to an outside service.” In other words, a hacker was able to obtain access to De Swardt’s account and was covertly siphoning off his tokens. Because account support tracks total usage but not itemized usage, even upon request, this kind of theft could have gone on for months undetected. He posted his experience on Reddit and after 80 comments, he discovered he was not alone. One person claimed that their account “was auto-upgraded without my consent, my credit card got charged, and the usage shot from 0% to 100% automatically without me even touching it.” Another saw usage go from 0 to 49% in 12 minutes, when all they had used it for was a couple of prompts and a web search. One Claude user said their account burned through its max tokens every day for three days without them using it at all; this person then created a GitHub report about it. Like with the Reddit post, other users shared similar experiences there, too. Two of them posted emails from Anthropic where the company had — to its credit — identified and warned them that their tokens were being stolen. “We have recently become aware of a bad actor that is using common infostealer malware to steal Claude login sessions from people’s computers, then using those login sessions to access Claude accounts and consume their usage,” the email read. Infostealers are a type of malware that installs itself on a user’s computer and steals saved passwords, session data, and login credentials. When Anthropic saw suspicious activity, it signed the users out, invalidated existing authorizations, issued some refunds, and warned them that they may have malware. The company also said the malware didn’t come from using Claude itself. Such malware can be picked up from many sources online, from downloading infected software to clicking on infected ads. Anthropic did not send De Swardt one of those emails. He insists he found no evidence that his computer was compromised and says he still has no way of determining how hackers gained access. De Swardt’s Claude account was reinstated after about two weeks. But the difficulty of getting speedy help for the matter, plus the lack of an itemized usage, soured him on Claude. He cancelled his subscription in favor of Cursor and its ability to use multiple models, including more affordable open source options. In his experience, these other models work as well as Claude. “It’s not that much different or better,” he said, adding that he can’t see going back “without [Anthropic] actually having resolved the issue in any way.” He says Anthropic still lacks tools that allow users to see what’s consuming their tokens. “I don’t think there’s any way that these people can protect themselves.” When asked for information on how users can identify misuse, Anthropic declined to comment.
impact: آسیب‌پذیری جدید در کلود امنیت حساب‌های پرداختی و تداوم کار کسب‌وکارهای وابسته به هوش مصنوعی را به خطر انداخته است.

title_fa: ارزش‌گذاری ۴۸ میلیارد دلاری سازنده Devin در جدیدترین دور سرمایه‌گذاری
title_en: Cognition hits $48B valuation, signaling investors believe AI coding is far from a winner-take-all market
summary: استارتاپ Cognition با جذب سرمایه ۲ میلیارد دلاری، ارزش خود را تنها در چهار ماه به ۴۸ میلیارد دلار رساند.
درآمد سالانه این شرکت سازنده دستیار برنامه‌نویسی Devin از ۴۹۲ میلیون دلار به ۹۰۰ میلیون دلار جهش یافته است.
سرمایه‌گذاران بزرگ برخلاف تصور انحصاری بودن بازار، هنوز شانس بالایی برای رقابت در حوزه کدنویسی هوش مصنوعی قائل هستند.
این شرکت برای کاهش هزینه‌های هنگفت سرورهای انویدیا، توسعه مدل‌های اختصاصی بر پایه نمونه‌های متن‌باز را آغاز کرده است.
full_text: Cognition, the startup developing coding assistant Devin, announced it raised $2 billion at a $48 billion valuation. The round, which comes just four months after Cognition’s previous fundraise at a $26 billion valuation, was led by Andreessen Horowitz, Accel, Founders Fund, General Catalyst, and Avenir. The startup’s soaring valuation signals that VCs still see room for multiple major players to capture meaningful market share in AI coding, one of the technology’s most significant applications. Cognition said that since announcing its last fundraise in May, its annualized run-rate revenue has grown from $492 million to $900 million. While the startup didn’t explain how it calculates that run-rate revenue, the metric is usually defined as a month’s top line multiplied by 12. Cursor, another popular coding assistant, was in talks in April to raise capital at a $50 billion valuation before agreeing to sell to SpaceX for $60 billion later that month. At the time of the funding talks, Cursor’s annualized revenue had surpassed $2 billion. This means Cognition currently commands a higher revenue multiple than Cursor did in the spring. Cursor ultimately sold to SpaceX largely because it was severely compute-constrained, according to investors familiar with its financials. It is unclear whether Cognition will face similar compute shortages. Cognition leases an Nvidia server cluster that costs hundreds of millions of dollars annually, which could push its total cash burn to $800 million this year, The Information reported. Like Cursor did before joining SpaceX, Cognition is training its own model based on open source alternatives. Over time, reducing its reliance on expensive third-party models from OpenAI and Anthropic will help cut costs and bring the company closer to breakeven. Cognition is expected to reach $4 billion to $5 billion in annualized revenue by the end of 2026, according to The Information. By comparison, TechCrunch reported in the spring that Cursor was on track to surpass $6 billion by year-end. Still, it’s notable that a16z, a major backer of Cursor, which made a killing when it sold to SpaceX, is back to lead a round in a Cursor competitor. Founded in 2024 by math prodigy Scott Wu, Cognition counts Mercedes-Benz, NASA, Goldman Sachs, and Citi among its major enterprise customers.
impact: رشد شتابان Cognition نشان‌دهنده رقابت سنگین و درآمدزایی فوق‌العاده در بازار دستیارهای هوش مصنوعی کدنویسی است.

title_fa: جذب سرمایه ۲۰ میلیون دلاری CloudNC برای هوشمندسازی تراشکاری صنعتی
title_en: CloudNC raises $20M to automate manufacturing’s most pressing bottlenecks
summary: استارتاپ بریتانیایی CloudNC با جذب ۲۰ میلیون دلار سرمایه جدید در دور مکمل B، مجموع سرمایه‌های دریافت‌کننده خود را به ۱۲۸ میلیون دلار رساند.
افزونه CAM Assist این شرکت به نرم‌افزارهای استاندارد صنعت مثل اتودسک متصل می‌شود تا فرایند پیچیده برنامه‌نویسی دستگاه‌های CNC را خودکار کند.
تمرکز اصلی این ابزار حذف نیروهای متخصص نیست، بلکه دستیاری هوشمند برای افزایش سرعت و حذف کارهای تکراری برنامه‌نویسان قطعات صنعتی است.
full_text: UK-based manufacturing software startup CloudNC announced a $20 million B extension round on Wednesday, bringing its lifetime total raised amount to $128 million. The company’s last major raise was four years ago, its co-founder and CEO Theo Saville told TechCrunch. Saville launched CloudNC in 2015 with Chris Emery, now the company’s chief science officer, and offers AI-powered CAM Assist software that automates parts of Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machining. CNC is the process of using computer-controlled machines to cut or shape materials precisely into the parts that are then used in automotive, defense, or consumer hardware industries. Before a part can be cut, Saville said, a machinist or a computer-aided manufacturing programmer has to decide issues like how a part should be held or what tools should be used, Saville said. They typically use powerful CAM software to help with this ideation phase, and although some of these tools can help users create part features or known part patterns, that’s different from looking at the part and generating an execution strategy an expert would actually want to use. “Traditional CAM systems are powerful, but in most workflows, they are still tools that allow programmers to manually specify how a part should be machined,” Saville said. This is where his CAM Assist comes in, a software that plugs into traditional CAM systems, like Autodesk Fusion or Mastercam, to help machinists and programmers make more efficient strategic manufacturing decisions. “It selects suitable tools, approach directions, and cutting feeds and speeds, and then drafts the code required to tell the CNC machine what to do,” Saville said. From there, the user reviews, edits, and approves the results. Saville said the goal was to help skilled workers be more “efficient and productive,” rather than removing expert judgment from the process. If “traditional CAM is a powerful toolkit,” he said, then “CAM Assist is more like an expert assistant sitting alongside the programmer, automating much of the first-pass thinking and repetitive setup so the human can review, improve, and approve the approach.” Saville said more than 1,000 machine shops worldwide use CAM Assist, and 80% of the company’s customer base, which includes both manufacturers and companies, is in the U.S. With a team of 80 employees, the company’s biggest goal is scaling adoption. “This makes this the right time to raise additional capital,” he said. Investors in the round include Nimble Ventures, which led the round, Calculus Venture Capital, Entrepreneur First, and LM Capital, Lockheed Martin’s venture arm. “The funding allows us to support wider take-up of CAM Assist, strengthen our go-to-market operations, expand in existing and new markets, and develop new products such as Quote Agent.” The premise behind Quote Agent, which targets manufacturers, is similar to CAM Assist. It helps shops assess the estimated cost and risk of a new project so they can move faster to accept — or reject — new work. He tied this somewhat back to geopolitics, pointing to, for example, how machine shops in the U.S. are looking to reshore and how, at the same time, there is a shortage of skilled workers in manufacturing. “Machine shops need to quote faster, program faster, and deliver more with the people and machines they already have,” he said, adding that Quote Agent is set to launch next month. “There are more ways to machine a typical CNC part than there are atoms in the universe,” he continued. “We have spent years attacking that specific problem, with our own factory, our own software team, and a lot of hard lessons from real machining. It’s been a long process to get to where we are today.”
impact: کاهش چشمگیر زمان برنامه‌نویسی قطعات صنعتی و تسریع فرایند تولید در صنایع خودروسازی و دفاعی.

title_en: From Dhoni to Sachin, Shilpa Shetty: Celebrities double down on startup bets
summary: گزارش جدید Tracxn نشان می‌دهد چهره‌های سرشناس هندی مایل به سرمایه‌گذاری مجدد روی شرکت‌های سبد قبلی خود هستند.

full_text: From Dhoni to Sachin, Shilpa Shetty: Celebrities double down on startup bets ADVERTISEMENT Indian celebrities are increasingly returning to startups they have already backed, rather than limiting their participation to one-off investments, according to a new report by private market intelligence platform Tracxn. The 10 celebrities tracked by Tracxn participated in 49 disclosed funding rounds across 34 India-headquartered startups between January 2021 and 2026 YTD, with the rounds carrying a combined disclosed value of around $458 million. The report, however, clarifies that the figure represents the total value of the funding rounds and not the amount invested by the celebrities themselves. The report ranks celebrities by the number of disclosed funding rounds they participated in and says it is “not a ranking of total capital invested or public profile”. Repeat bets account for nearly half of rounds The biggest trend emerging from the data is the extent to which celebrities have continued backing companies already present in their portfolios. Nine celebrity-company pairs accounted for 22 of the 49 disclosed rounds, meaning nearly 45% of all rounds involved repeat participation by the same celebrity in the same company. Cricketer Sachin Tendulkar stands out with five disclosed rounds in used-car platform Spinny between 2021 and 2025. His participation includes Spinny's $250 million Series E round in November 2021, followed by four further disclosed rounds between September 2022 and September 2025. Actor Shilpa Shetty Kundra, who tops the overall ranking with 10 rounds, participated in three separate funding rounds in food and beverage startup WickedGud and two rounds in online grocery platform KisanKonnect. The report notes that where a celebrity invested in the same company across multiple funding rounds, “each round is listed as a separate entry in the table.” Shilpa Shetty leads celebrity investor ranking Shetty leads the list with 10 disclosed rounds, followed by MS Dhoni and Sachin Tendulkar with six each. Shraddha Kapoor and Virat Kohli have five rounds each, while Alia Bhatt and Anushka Sharma have four each. Ranveer Singh, Rohit Sharma and Suniel Shetty have three disclosed rounds apiece. Dhoni's investments cover a wider range of sectors, including solar energy, drones, electric vehicles, fitness, food technology and OTT video. His latest disclosed investment in the period was a $53 million Series C round in SolarSquare in June 2026. Anushka Sharma also remained active in 2026, participating in a $24 million Series C round in footwear company Agilitas in May. Celebrity capital tends to enter early The report also shows a preference for early-stage startup funding. Of the 49 disclosed rounds, 27 or 55% were Angel or Seed rounds, while another 13 were Series A. The 34 startups span sectors including food and beverage, beauty and personal care, fashion, mobility, education, logistics, drones and solar energy. Maharashtra accounted for 15 of the startups, including 12 in Mumbai, followed by Haryana with six, Karnataka with five and Delhi with three. Several celebrity-backed companies have also progressed to major liquidity or ownership events. Five of the 34 companies have reached an acquisition or public-listing event, including Mamaearth, Klassroom, Ed-a-Mamma, Shunya and Purple Style Labs.

summary: کاربران پلن‌های ۱۰۰ تا ۲۰۰ دلاری Max مدعی شده‌اند که محدودیت‌های مصرف واقعی بسیار کمتر از تبلیغات «۵ تا ۲۰ برابر پلن پرو» است.

full_text: Anthropic says power users are key to its business — it’s prioritized them even when it means cutting off other popular applications, like OpenClaw. But some of these same customers say Anthropic misled them into believing they’d get more out of a top-tier pricing subscription than they did. A new class action lawsuit questions whether Anthropic broke the law by misleading power users Subscribers of Anthropic’s Max plan ($100-$200 per month) say they didn’t get what they thought they were paying for. A new class action lawsuit questions whether Anthropic broke the law by misleading power users Subscribers of Anthropic’s Max plan ($100-$200 per month) say they didn’t get what they thought they were paying for. In an expanded class action lawsuit filed today, a group of Claude subscribers say the company deceptively advertised the limits of its Max subscription tier. The lawsuit was brought by attorneys Monica Vaca and Kati Daffan, who both formerly worked at the Federal Trade Commission under Lina Khan. It’s a rare attempt to legally penalize AI companies for a widely held point of frustration: the industry’s growing money squeeze. Anthropic’s Max plan for Claude is an upgrade to the $20/month Pro plan. It has two pricing options: $100 per month for “5x” the usage limits of Pro or $200 per month for “20x”. But the lawsuit alleges that these numbers, advertised in Anthropic’s marketing graphics, are misleadingly couched in fine print. Anthropic actually says you’ll get 20x or 5x the usage that the Pro plan offers, but it’s only promised for five-hour chunks of time that are subject to a weekly limit — which the complaint alleges adds up to a much smaller total increase in usage capacity. To understand this, “you’ve got to dive deep,” Vaca said. It requires clicking two different hyperlinks to see the word “session,” and then to see what “session” meant, you’d need to separately go to the Pro plan webpage for an expanded definition. Complaints about Max’s terms have cropped up online. One Reddit user wrote, “The weekly allowance is what the pricing page makes you think you’re buying. The rolling 5-hour window is what actually controls whether you can work … It’s like giving someone a bigger gas tank while keeping the fuel pump limited to one gallon every five hours.” Vaca said in an interview that Claude users often will upgrade on the fly if they encounter limits while working on a project, then are often frustrated after they pay. “People see that they are going to get this dramatically expanded usage … What we hear from people, though, is that when they sign up, they are surprised that they’re not getting the usage that they thought they were getting.” Over the past eight months or more, as pressures to turn a profit increase, AI customers have frequently complained that top labs are passing on their steep operating costs. Although Anthropic announced the Max plan in April 2025, it didn’t impose the allegedly deceptive weekly limits until a few months later in August, as the company pushed to compete with OpenAI. In Anthropic’s latest model release, Fable 5.1, the company hinted at broader cost concerns among customers, writing that it was “addressing the feedback we’ve received from customers on price” in the new model’s pricing. The complaint was filed in July before being withdrawn and refiled as an expanded class action. In a motion to dismiss the earlier case, Anthropic argued that it didn’t necessarily omit the session limits from its marketing; rather, it says it’s technically available to the consumer if they know where to look. “Accessing this clarifying information … required nothing more than clicking hyperlinks available in the purchase process—the digital equivalent of flipping a product over to read the back label,” Anthropic wrote in the motion to dismiss. Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment. Vaca disagrees that it’s that easy to understand the terms. “This is hard for consumers — they don’t know what’s in that black box,” she said. “They have to rely on the claims the marketer is giving. There’s no way for them to audit it. There’s no way for them to know exactly what it is they’re going to get… They’re basically taking a leap, and they’re believing in an honest marketplace.” She added that another reason the case was “compelling” for her is that she and Daffan started hearing from people who felt they needed to pay high-priced subscription costs for AI services in order to avoid becoming irrelevant in the job market. But oftentimes, she said, they felt they weren’t getting what they paid for, which was frustrating for a service that costs between $100 and $200 per month. “[Daffan] and I worked at the Federal Trade Commission for 38 years combined,” Vaca said, adding, “There is a long line of precedent on false advertising. It’s commercial speech. You can’t lie when you’re marketing a product.” Even if Anthropic has the stipulations somewhere on its website, Vaca said, it shouldn’t be up to the consumer to have to seek that out. “It’s a ‘buyer beware’ approach,” she said. “And that’s really not fair to people.”

title_en: Tellia Raises $5 Million to Bring Voice AI to Farm Fields
summary: استارتاپ تلیه با جذب سرمایه ۵ میلیون دلاری، ابزار هوش مصنوعی صوتی خود را برای ثبت اطلاعات زمین‌های کشاورزی توسعه می‌دهد.
کشاورزان به جای پر کردن فرم‌های پیچیده، فقط با صحبت کردن یا فرستادن ویس، داده‌های زراعی را ثبت و مدیریت می‌کنند.
این سیستم در آمریکا و اروپا وارد فاز عملیاتی شده و نرخ استفاده روزانه آن به ۸۰ درصد رسیده است.
full_text: Key Takeaways - Tellia, a voice AI startup for agriculture, has raised $5 million in pre-seed funding to expand a platform that turns spoken field updates into structured data. - The round was led by Revent, with participation from Grey Silo Ventures (the corporate venture arm of Cereal Docks Group), Jeriko (operated by Techmind) and Fund F. - Users record information through phone calls, texts, voice notes, WhatsApp or email, and Tellia converts it into records tied to the right field, crop and crew. - In the US, the product reaches 80% daily active usage within two months of onboarding, with deployments at Campos Brothers Farms and Duckhorn wineries. - In Europe, Tellia is live with the Institut Français de la Vigne et du Vin (IFV), the cooperative Val de Gascogne and German plant breeder KWS Saat. Tellia Closes $5 Million Pre-Seed Round Tellia, a voice AI assistant built for agriculture, has raised $5 million in pre-seed funding to scale technology that lets farmers, agronomists and field teams capture and use their data by speaking. Announced on 8 September 2026 from San Francisco and Paris, the round was led by European venture firm Revent, with participation from Grey Silo Ventures, the corporate venture capital arm of Cereal Docks Group, Jeriko, an investment club operated by Techmind, and Fund F. Closing the Gap Between the Field and the Software Much of the software written for farming still depends on screens, forms and manual entry designed for the office rather than the field. Details from daily work, such as disease sightings, spray decisions, scouting notes and crew updates, often stay in notebooks, messaging threads or memory. Tellia adds a voice layer that captures information in natural language and turns it into structured records connected to the right field, crop, crew and operation, while letting users ask operational and agronomic questions and get instant answers. Rather than forcing teams into a fixed template, the system shapes its structure around how each farm runs. “The Ag industry keeps facing the same challenge: the people who spend their days in the field spend their evenings at a keyboard,” said Coline Labadie de Faÿ, CEO and co-founder of Tellia. “That was never a data problem. It was an interface problem. Traditional software cannot accept it the way it actually comes out, spoken, in the field, in whatever language the team works in. So we did not build another platform that wants to own all the data. Instead, we built the interface. You talk, Tellia captures it, structures it, and interprets it into something the whole operation can act on. This funding round lets us push the voice AI further, build the agentic layer that sits between the field and the rest of the agtech stack, and grow our team in the US and Europe.” Early Deployments Across the US and Europe The company launched first in the US, where it reports 80% daily active usage among field teams within two months of onboarding. Its San Francisco operations have supported work with almond producer Campos Brothers Farms and the Duckhorn wineries. In Europe, Tellia is deployed with the Institut Français de la Vigne et du Vin (IFV), the cooperative Val de Gascogne and German plant breeder KWS Saat. The company plans to use the funding to build an agentic layer that partners can embed through an API, so records and recommendations appear inside a partner’s own product. Investors Back Tellia’s Voice-First Approach “We believe that the voice first approach will lead the agricultural sector into the new agentic data age and that Tellia will be the category defining company here,” said Otto Birnbaum, general partner at Revent. “Tellia is creating the critical data layer to meaningfully improve efficiencies and productivity in the agricultural sector. We are thrilled to partner with Coline and Vincent and are deeply impressed by their operational pace and how fast the product gets adopted on both sides of the Atlantic.” Tellia’s founders met through Entrepreneur First and now run the 13-person company on both sides of the Atlantic, pairing US commercial traction with European standards on data protection and security. The company says its long-term aim is to become the main voice interface between agriculture and the technology that supports it.
impact: دیجیتالی‌شدن آسان داده‌های کشاورزی بدون نیاز به تایپ دستی و حذف فرم‌های کاغذی.

title_fa: تغییر استراتژی گوگل؛ انتشار بروزرسانی‌های کروم دو هفته‌ای شد
title_en: Chrome is now shipping updates every 2 weeks as AI changes the security landscape
summary: گوگل چرخه آپدیت کروم را از چهار هفته به دو هفته کاهش داد تا به تهدیدات امنیتی عصر هوش مصنوعی سریع‌تر پاسخ دهد.
این اقدام فاصله زمانی انتشار وصله‌های امنیتی (N-day gap) را برای بستن منافذ نفوذ به حداقل می‌رساند.
سرعت بالای عرضه فیچرهای جدید به کروم کمک می‌کند در برابر مرورگرهای هوشمند جدید بازار رقابت کند.
full_text: Chrome has officially switched from a four- to a two-week release schedule, as Google promised earlier this year, with Tuesday’s launch of Chrome 153 on desktop, iOS, and Android. The shift to faster releases is tied to Chrome’s evolving security strategy in the AI era, the company explained. As automated AI tools and community bug reports have pushed up the volume of patches and updates, Google says that a shorter release cycle makes it easier to manage security fixes. This is also critical because faster-moving threats, some of which can also be attributed to AI, can be better addressed by shrinking the window between landing a fix in the public codebase and getting that fix to end users, the company notes. A shorter release schedule would help keep the “N-day” patch gap — the gap between when a security vulnerability is known and when it gets patched — as small as possible. Faster releases have another benefit, too: They can help Chrome ship features faster. This is also key in the AI era, as AI-assisted software development has enabled a host of new browser competitors to emerge. While OpenAI’s web browser, ChatGPT Atlas, has been shut down, there are still plenty of other alternative browsers looking to carve out a piece of Chrome’s market for themselves, including Brave, Dia, Opera Neon, Perplexity’s Comet, DuckDuckGo’s browser, and more. Plus, Google is experimenting with adding more AI features to Chrome and then rapidly iterating on those additions, which also demands faster updates. The move to a two-week release schedule benefits the broader web as well. Because of Chrome’s position as the most-used browser globally, such changes can help set the standard for the industry. Mozilla, Microsoft, and Brave have already begun adopting a faster two-week schedule, following Chrome’s lead. This is not the first time Chrome has adjusted its release schedule to enable faster patch management. The company first moved to a four-week release cycle in 2021, down from six weeks, after establishing its principles of “release early, release often” over a decade prior.
impact: ارتقای سطح امنیت صدها میلیون کاربر و بازتعریف استاندارد بروزرسانی در کل صنعت مرورگرها.

title_fa: معماری جدید Arm برای اجرای هوش مصنوعی روی موبایل
title_en: پلتفرم پردازشی جدید آرم برای اجرای ایجنت‌های هوش مصنوعی روی موبایل معرفی شد
summary: شرکت Arm پلتفرم جدید CSS for Mobile 2 را با تمرکز بر اجرای آفلاین ایجنت‌های هوش مصنوعی و پردازش گرافیکی سنگین معرفی کرد.
استفاده از هسته‌ پردازشی C2-Ultra و دو واحد SME2 سرعت اجرای مدل‌های زبانی کوچک را تا ۷۰ درصد افزایش می‌دهد.
پردازنده گرافیکی Mali G2-Ultra NX امکان اجرای بازی‌های گرافیکی پیشرفته را با مصرف انرژی بسیار پایین ۱ وات فراهم می‌سازد.
full_text: آرم (Arm) پلتفرم جدیدی برای موبایل معرفی کرد که با تمرکز بر اجرای ایجنتهای هوش مصنوعی روی دستگاه و ارائه گرافیک با کیفیت در سطح سیستمهای دسکتاپ طراحی شده است. این شرکت میگوید معماری جدید میتواند اجرای بازیهای گرافیکی سنگین را در محدوده مصرف انرژی یک وات ممکن کند. این پلتفرم با نام Compute Subsystem (CSS) for Mobile 2 در رویداد Arm Everywhere China در شانگهای معرفی شد و جایگزین پلتفرم Lumex CSS سال گذشته میشود. آرم این محصول را بخشی از راهبرد خود برای توسعه در حوزه هوش مصنوعی میداند. پلتفرم جدید آرم برای اجرای ایجنتهای هوش مصنوعی به گفته آرم، بخش قابلتوجهی از کارهای هوش مصنوعی همچنان در فضای ابری اجرا میشوند؛ وابستگی هر تعامل به رفتوبرگشت دادهها میان دستگاه و مرکز داده میتواند بر تأخیر، اتصال شبکه و هزینه ارائه سرویسها در مقیاس بزرگ تأثیر بگذارد. همین موضوع باعث حرکت پردازشها به سمت توزیع بیشتر و اجرای آنها در لبه شبکه میشود. آرم میگوید هوش مصنوعی حالا به ابزارهایی تبدیل شده است که کاربران مستقیماً با آنها تعامل دارند؛ ایجنتهای هوش مصنوعی اکنون میتوانند هدف کاربر را تفسیر، اپلیکیشنها و مدلها را هماهنگ و مجموعهای از اقدامات را اجرا کنند. چنین فرایندی شامل استنتاجهای مکرر، منطق برنامه، هماهنگسازی سیستم و اجرای همزمان چند کار است. به همین دلیل، تنها افزایش عملکرد CPU کافی نیست و به چند هسته پردازشی قدرتمند نیاز است تا بارهای کاری مختلف همزمان اجرا شوند. پلتفرم CSS for Mobile 2 از خوشه پردازشی جدید C2 استفاده میکند که در بالاترین سطح آن هسته C2-Ultra قرار دارد. آرم ادعا میکند این هسته در عملکرد تکرشتهای تا ۱۵ درصد سریعتر از هسته C1-Ultra در پلتفرم سال گذشته است. C2-Ultra به موتور اجرای بزرگتری مجهز شده است تا بتواند دستورهای بیشتری را همزمان در حال پردازش نگه دارد. آرم همچنین از بهبود پیشبینی انشعاب و پیشبینی دریافت و مقصد دستورها برای تغذیه بهتر خط لوله پردازشی خبر داده است. شرکتهای تولیدکننده تراشه میتوانند مانند گذشته اجزای مختلف این پلتفرم را براساس نیاز خود ترکیب کنند. آرم برای پیکربندی پرچمدار، دو هسته C2-Ultra، شش هسته کممصرف C2-Pro و دو واحد SME2 را پیشنهاد میکند. پلتفرم سال گذشته تنها یک واحد SME2 داشت. آرم میگوید دو برابر شدن ظرفیت SME2 میتواند سرعت اجرای مدلهای زبانی کوچک جدید را تا ۷۰ درصد افزایش دهد. این خوشه همچنین از حافظههای کش خصوصی برای سیپییوهای مجزا و یک کش بزرگ اشتراکی L3 بهره میبرد که اجزای آن از طریق DynamIQ Shared Unit به یکدیگر متصل میشوند. آرم در GPU جدید (Mali G2-Ultra NX) از سختافزار اختصاصی هوش مصنوعی برای پردازش گرافیک استفاده کرده است. این GPU همچنین به موتور پردازشی جدید و نسل سوم رهگیری پرتو مجهز شده تا بتواند نور و سایهها را در صحنههای بازی پردازش کند. یکی از قابلیتهای اصلی این GPU، فناوری NSS است. این فناوری به GPU امکان میدهد بازی را با وضوح ۵۴۰p رندر کند و سپس با کمک سختافزار هوش مصنوعی، تصویر را به ۱۰۸۰p بازسازی کند. به این ترتیب، GPU لازم نیست تمام تصویر نهایی را با وضوح کامل پردازش کند. فناوری دیگری به نام NFRU نیز با استفاده از هوش مصنوعی، فریمهای میانی را تولید میکند. بنابراین بخشی از فریمهایی که بازیکن روی نمایشگر میبیند، مستقیماً توسط GPU رندر نمیشوند و سختافزار عصبی آنها را ایجاد میکند. آرم میگوید ترکیب NSS و NFRU باعث میشود GPU برای تولید خروجی نهایی، تنها حدود یکهشتم پیکسلها را بهصورت مستقیم رندر کند و سختافزار عصبی بقیه تصویر را بازسازی کند.
impact: کاهش وابستگی گوشی‌ها به پردازش ابری و افزایش سرعت پاسخ‌دهی ایجنت‌های هوشمند روی دستگاه.

title_fa: پشتیبانی واتس‌اپ از ۵ ایجنت هوش مصنوعی شخص ثالث
title_en: واتس‌اپ قابلیت اتصال حداکثر پنج ایجنت هوش مصنوعی شخص ثالث را فراهم می‌کند
summary: واتس‌اپ قابلیت جدیدی را تست می‌کند که به کاربران اجازه می‌دهد ۵ ایجنت هوش مصنوعی دلخواه را از طریق کلید API متصل کنند.
امکان تنظیم نام و عکس پروفایل مجزا برای هر ایجنت وجود دارد و گفت‌وگوها در چت‌های اختصاصی انجام می‌شوند.
این ایجنت‌ها فقط به محتوای همان چت دسترسی دارند، اما پیام‌ها هنوز از رمزنگاری سرتاسری پشتیبانی نمی‌کنند.
full_text: واتساپ درحال توسعه قابلیتی است که به کاربران امکان میدهد ایجنتهای هوش مصنوعی شخص ثالث را به این پیامرسان متصل، با آنها گفتوگو کنند و دستور انجام وظایف مختلف را به آنها بدهند. این قابلیت درحالحاضر برای برخی کاربران اندروید در دسترس قرار گرفته است. پس از افزایش محبوبیت پلتفرمهایی مانند OpenClaw، یکی از روشهای رایج برای تعامل از راه دور با ایجنتهای هوش مصنوعی، اتصال آنها به اپلیکیشنهای پیامرسان بود. بااینحال، برخی کاربران دریافتند که راهاندازی بات برای ارتباط با ایجنتهای هوش مصنوعی شخص ثالث در واتساپ میتواند به مسدودشدن حساب کاربری منجر شود. در مقابل، تلگرام این روند را پذیرفت و به یکی از پلتفرمهایی تبدیل شد که کاربران برای گفتوگو با ایجنتهایی که روی کامپیوتر یا فضای ابری اجرا میشوند، به سراغ آنها میروند. حالا طبق گزارش WABetaInfo، واتساپ درحال اضافهکردن پشتیبانی داخلی از ایجنتهای شخص ثالث است. این قابلیت به کاربران امکان میدهد ایجنت موردنظر خود را مستقیماً به چت اختصاصی واتساپ متصل کنند. قابلیت فعلی واتساپ از حداکثر پنج ایجنت برای هر حساب پشتیبانی میکند. کاربران همچنین میتوانند برای هر ایجنت نام و تصویر پروفایل جداگانه تعیین کنند. بااینحال، چتهای مربوط به ایجنتهای شخص ثالث درحالحاضر از رمزنگاری سرتاسری برخوردار نیستند. دسترسی ایجنت هوش مصنوعی در واتساپ برای راهاندازی ایجنت، واتساپ پس از ایجاد بات جدید، یک کلید API در اختیار کاربر قرار میدهد. کاربر میتواند این کلید را در سرویس مربوط به ایجنت وارد کند. مراحل دقیق اتصال بسته به پلتفرم مورد استفاده متفاوت است، اما به گفته WABetaInfo، بیشتر سرویسها محلی برای واردکردن این کلید دارند. پس از اتصال، کاربر میتواند گفتوگوی اختصاصی ایجنت را در واتساپ باز کند، برای آن پیام بفرستد و پاسخها را مستقیماً در همان اپلیکیشن دریافت کند. طبق توضیحات WABetaInfo، ایجنت متصلشده فقط میتواند محتوایی را بخواند که کاربر در همان گفتوگو با آن به اشتراک گذاشته است. بنابراین، این ایجنتها به سایر مکالمات، مخاطبان یا فایلهای رسانهای حساب کاربر دسترسی ندارند. در وضعیت فعلی، این قابلیت فقط از چتهای فردی پشتیبانی میکند و امکان افزودن ایجنتها به گروهها یا کامیونیتیهای واتساپ وجود ندارد. واتساپ همچنین هشدار میدهد اگر ایجنت متصلشده مبتنی بر هوش مصنوعی باشد، پاسخهای آن ممکن است نادرست باشند. بنابراین، کاربران باید اطلاعاتی را که ایجنت ارائه میکند بررسی کنند. این قابلیت فعلاً برای گروهی از کاربران اندروید فعال شده و انتظار میرود در آینده نزدیک دسترسی به آن گستردهتر شود.
impact: تسهیل اتوماسیون کارهای روزمره کاربران و ورود رسمی واتس‌اپ به رقابت با تلگرام در حوزه بات‌های هوشمند.

title_fa: جذب سرمایه ۵۰ میلیون دلاری استارتاپ نیروگاه‌های هسته‌ای شناور
title_en: Nuclear startup Bluecore Energy raises $50M seed round, just two months after launch
summary: استارتاپ Bluecore Energy دو ماه پس از اعلام حضور، ۵۰ میلیون دلار سرمایه جدید جذب کرد.
این شرکت رآکتورهای هسته‌ای کوچک را روی بارج‌های شناور می‌سازد تا برق پاک بنادر و مراکز داده ساحلی را تامین کند.
ارزیابی طرح توسط نهادهای تنظیم‌کننده آمریکا آغاز شده تا زمان احداث نیروگاه از چند سال به چند روز کاهش یابد.
full_text: Bluecore Energy announced Tuesday an oversubscribed $50 million seed round — just months after raising a $10 million pre-seed and coming out of stealth. As TechCrunch previously reported, the company, founded earlier this year by Kofi Asante, builds small nuclear reactors (SMRs) on floating barges, rather than fixed locations, to generate clean energy for ports and nearby infrastructure. This means that energy can be transported to wherever it is needed, an idea Asante hopes can bring clean power to those who need it most. “The Navy is doing this as we speak, for the last 70 years, and has never had an accident,” Asante said about the use of portable technology in a new interview with TechCrunch. “We just made it smaller, so you can actually move things around in a way that doesn’t take years” — or a new set of infrastructure — ”but days.” Asante wasn’t planning on fundraising this year, but calls kept coming after their pre-seed launch. Many of their pre-seed investors, including Slauson & Co., Harlem Capital, and Ripple co-founder Chris Larsen, doubled down on this new round, with new capital coming from investors like Collab Capital, Kevin Hart’s HartBeat Ventures, and angel investors from Tesla, Uber, Amazon, and Google. Silverton Partners led this new seed round, and it took eight weeks to close. “I just kept having to figure out a way to make more room” — on the cap table, Asante said. “I wasn’t anticipating us raising that level of capital in that period of time, but really fortunate that we have so many investors and partners who are excited.” When it emerged from stealth in July, it became the first nuclear company headquartered at a major port: the Port of Long Beach. It has since launched two floating barges and has struck a partnership with the Department of Transportation Maritime Division, the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), and the U.S. Coast Guard. Bluecore Energy is now undergoing review with the NRC and the Coast Guard on its product design, which, if successful, will lead to certification of its floating nuclear power plant. “We have been talking to them both since the inception of the company and design, but officially started the formal engagement in August,” Asante said. The fresh capital will fund continued product development, regulatory work, nuclear fuel purchases, and hiring. Asante anticipates the biggest challenge to be the supply chain, securing hardware to build the right portable electricity infrastructure at a pace that can match consumer demand. He said that Bluecore Energy has seen inbound interest from “multiple ports, AI data centers and communities that need clean energy and water.” “Our team comes from SpaceX, Rivian, and Toyota, so we are applying similar strategies to be able to secure critical parts,” he said. “We already have barges and a reactor and are now about to order nuclear fuel to go to our partner at a national nuclear lab.” It all goes back to the core mission, Asante said, “to democratize access to clean energy.” “My philosophy is that access to clean energy and also clean water should be a human right,” he said.
impact: تحول در تامین انرژی پاک و سیار برای زیرساخت‌های بزرگ بدون نیاز به تملک زمین و ساخت‌وساز طولانی.

title_fa: رکوردشکنی بی‌سابقه مایکروسافت در ترمیم باگ‌های ویندوز با کمک مدل‌های AI
title_en: Microsoft breaks another patch Tuesday record
summary: کشف سریع آسیب‌پذیری‌ها توسط مدل‌های جدید هوش مصنوعی، مایکروسافت را به انتشار بیش از ۶۵۰ وصله امنیتی در یک روز وادار کرد.
حجم اصلاحات امنیتی ویندوز نسبت به دوران پیش از ورود مدل‌های هوش مصنوعی شش برابر شده است.
مایکروسافت پیش از سوءاستفاده هکرها از مدل‌های هوش مصنوعی، با تمام توان در حال شناسایی رخنه نرم‌افزارهای خود است.
این حجم بی‌سابقه به‌روزرسانی فشار کاری شدیدی را به تیم‌های پشتیبانی فنی و مدیران شبکه وارد کرده است.
full_text: Engineers at Microsoft typically enjoy a quieter summer to take vacations and spend time with family, as is common at many companies. But this year, the season has been unusually busy for Windows and security engineers, thanks to new AI models that are discovering software vulnerabilities at a rapid pace. Sources tell me that Microsoft will set another patch Tuesday record today, the third in just a few months. Microsoft breaks another patch Tuesday record Windows and security engineers have had a busy summer. Windows and security engineers have had a busy summer. It all kicked off in April when Anthropic’s new Mythos model found security vulnerabilities in “every major operating system and web browser.” A few weeks later, OpenAI released its own cybersecurity-focused model to trusted partners. Sources familiar with Microsoft’s security work tell me both of these models have contributed to a record-breaking series of patch Tuesdays over the summer period. Microsoft typically patches around 100 flaws every month, but in June it set a new record of around 200 fixes. July’s patch Tuesday was even bigger, with Microsoft patching at least 570 security holes, almost triple the number of June’s record-breaking release. Microsoft engineers had a chance to catch their breath a bit in August when they plugged nearly 400 security vulnerabilities. I understand today’s September patch Tuesday is about to set a new record, with more than 650 security fixes for Windows alone. That’s six times the number that usually got patched before the AI models arrived. Engineers have been busy over the summer verifying fixes for hundreds of important patches, which include remote code vulnerabilities, privilege escalations, and more. As Microsoft uses more and more security-focused AI models to discover software vulnerabilities, the number of flaws that need patching keeps increasing. While today’s patch Tuesday is another record-breaking event, I wouldn’t be surprised to see this record broken again — particularly if there’s another model advance soon. Like many other software companies, Microsoft is urgently hunting for vulnerabilities before the advances in AI let malicious actors exploit undiscovered weaknesses in Windows, Azure, and other software. While Microsoft is issuing an unusual number of fixes, the sheer amount is also putting pressure on businesses that rely on Microsoft’s software to apply the patches as soon as possible. IT admins typically have to test patches from Microsoft to ensure any fixes don’t interfere with critical business applications. This process can create what’s called a “patch gap” between a vulnerability being disclosed and people applying the fix. In an AI era of security vulnerabilities being rapidly discovered and disclosed, there’s a huge amount of pressure on businesses to close the patch gap. Anthropic discovered earlier this year that Mythos could even create working exploits for newly disclosed software vulnerabilities in a matter of hours, instead of weeks. This puts businesses at risk of being hit by an exploit if they don’t patch soon enough. It’s particularly risky if Microsoft discovers remote code vulnerabilities that are easy for hackers to exploit. The patch gap has always been a risk in cybersecurity, but with the sheer volume of vulnerabilities being discovered in the AI era, I’m sure we’ll see Microsoft and others warning companies once again to apply patches as soon as they’re released. When hundreds of vulnerabilities are now being discovered every month, time is very much of the essence. Forza Horizon 6 isn’t racing onto the PS5 this year Microsoft is planning to delay the release of Forza Horizon 6 on PS5, according to sources familiar with Playground Games’ plans. While the game was initially announced as coming to PS5 later this year, I understand there’s going to be a slight delay, pushing it into early 2027. Forza Horizon 6 has been hugely popular on Xbox and PC, and the previous instalment of the series, Forza Horizon 5, proved popular on PS5, after Microsoft released it on Sony’s console last year. I understand that the PS5 release delay is more about lining up with the first expansion for Forza Horizon 6, than anything else. Forza Horizon 6 first debuted on Xbox and PC on May 15th, and I’m expecting it to launch on PS5 ahead of the 12-month anniversary mark. Microsoft is getting ready to roll out its memory integrity security feature for Windows 11 to more devices next month. The kernel-level protection feature is designed to stop malicious code or drivers running on a Windows 11 machine, but it also impacts PC gaming performance on certain CPUs. There’s less of an impact if you have a more modern CPU, but you might notice more of a frame-rate drop in select games on older processors. Microsoft won’t automatically enable memory integrity again next month if you’ve already previously disabled the feature. - Microsoft is turning off text predictions in Word and Outlook. It turns out that a lot of people hate text predictions in Word and Outlook, so Microsoft is turning them off by default. The feature was supposed to help you write documents and emails faster by guessing what word you’d type next, but Microsoft’s predictive text could often be more of a distraction. The change is rolling out on Word for Windows, iOS, and Android, as well as Outlook on Windows and Mac. - Microsoft discloses Azure revenue as part of major financial reporting changes. Microsoft is changing how it reports its finances to investors by splitting its businesses into two segments and disclosing quarterly revenue for its Azure cloud business for the first time. title_fa: ادغام کامل هوش مصنوعی در پریمیر؛ ساخت ویدیو و صدا روی تایم‌لاین
title_en: Adobe is trying to make its AI generators idiot-proof in Premiere
summary: ابزار جدید Generative Media در پریمیر امکان ساخت ویدیو، موزیک و افکت صوتی را بدون خروج از تایم‌لاین فراهم کرده است.
تدوین‌گران می‌توانند مستقیماً از مدل‌های پیشرفته‌ای چون Google Veo، Runway، Luma، Kling و Firefly استفاده کنند.
ابزارهای صوتی هوشمند جدید امکان تفکیک گویندگان و تنظیم خودکار صدای پس‌زمینه را میسر می‌سازند.
full_text: Adobe is overhauling how editors interact with AI in its Premiere professional video editing software. Its new Generative Media tool makes it easier to generate video, sound effects, music, and soundscapes without ever leaving the project timeline. The generators themselves aren’t entirely new; the big change is how easily you can access them without breaking your workflow. Adobe is trying to make its AI generators idiot-proof in Premiere A dedicated Generative Media interface can now be accessed right from the project timeline. A dedicated Generative Media interface can now be accessed right from the project timeline. Instead of jumping between browsers or external apps to find missing B-roll or audio elements, editors can now highlight an empty gap on the video or audio track and generate context-aware, fully editable clips without leaving the project. Editors can choose from multiple underlying models directly in the timeline — including Adobe Firefly, Google Veo, Runway, Luma, and Kling — to best match their project’s style. Premiere is also getting new AI audio tools (in beta) that can separate overlapping speakers, automatically duck music under speech, and independently adjust dialogue and ambience. And Adobe is bringing its AI Assistant to After Effects (also in beta) that lets editors use plain-language commands to reorganize projects, fix technical problems, and create effects without writing expressions themselves.
impact: تسریع چشمگیر فرآیند تدوین ویدیو و بی‌نیاز شدن تدوین‌گران از ابزارهای خارجی.

title_fa: واقعیت نمایشگاه الکامپ و چالش‌های زیرساختی استارتاپ‌های ایرانی
title_en: از عکس‌های یادگاری وزیر تا خاموشی سرورها؛ الکامپ واقعاً چه چیزی به استارتاپ‌ها می‌دهد؟
summary: حضور مقامات در الکامپ بیشتر جنبه تبلیغاتی دارد و چالش‌های کلیدی کسب‌وکارها مانند قطعی اینترنت را حل نمی‌کند.
فضای استارتاپی کشور با افت هیجان روبه‌رو شده و غرفه‌ها بیشتر به سمت فروش سرویس‌های آماده حرکت کرده‌اند.
با وجود تمام مشکلات، الکامپ همچنان فرصتی غنیمت برای شبکه‌سازی B2B و ایجاد تعاملات کاری میان شرکت‌ها است.
full_text: وزیر ارتباطات سال گذشته در الکامپ به غرفه یک کسبوکار حوزه هوش مصنوعی رفت، با تیم این کسبوکار صحبت کرد و چند دقیقهای مقابل دوربینها ایستاد. چند ماه بعد، همان کسبوکاری که در نمایشگاه محصولش را معرفی میکرد، بهدلیل قطعی طولانی اینترنت ناچار شد سرورهایش را خاموش کند و بنیانگذارانش برای دسترسی به اینترنت پایدار از ایران خارج شدند. این فاصله میان حضور سیاستگذار در ویترین فناوری و واقعیت کسبوکارها، امسال در پاویون هوش مصنوعی الکامپ هم به شکل دیگری قابل مشاهده بود؛ جایی که در مقایسه با سال گذشته، بخش کمتری از شرکتها راهکارهایی برای حل مسائل واقعی کسبوکارها با هوش مصنوعی ارائه میکردند و تعداد بیشتری از غرفهها به سرویسهای آماده یا فروش دسترسی به مدلهای هوش مصنوعی اختصاص داشتند. اما الکامپ واقعا چه چیزی به استارتاپها میدهد؟ فرزانه برکت مومنی، همبنیانگذار دوات درباره بازدید وزیر، اتفاقی را که در ظاهر میتوانست یکی از نقاط مهم حضور یک استارتاپ در الکامپ باشد، چندان جدی نمیداند و آن را در یک جمله خلاصه میکند: «فقط یک دوپامین لحظهای ایجاد کرد.» به گفته او، موج دوربینها و توجهی که همزمان با حضور وزیر ایجاد شد، بعد از پایان بازدید اثر مشخصی بر کسبوکار نداشت و عکسها و ویدئوهای آن بیشتر برای استفاده در شبکههای اجتماعی شرکت باقی ماندند. فردی هم از جمعیت به سراغشان آمده و پیشنهاد فروش ویدئوی باکیفیت بازدید وزیر با قیمت ۴ میلیون تومان را به آنها داده است. این شاید پاسخ روشنی به یکی از تصورات رایج درباره حضور سیاستگذاران در نمایشگاههای فناوری باشد. حضور یک مقام در غرفه میتواند برای چند دقیقه یک کسبوکار را در مرکز توجه قرار دهد، اما لزوماً مسئلهای از مسائل واقعی آن کسبوکار را حل نمیکند. ارزش حضور در الکامپ این شرکت که مدل کسبوکارش B2B است، حضور سایر کسبوکارهای دیجیتال را یکی از مهمترین دلایل ارزشمند بودن نمایشگاه میدانست. مدیران شرکت، علاوه بر حضور در غرفه خود، فرصت داشتند میان غرفهها حرکت کنند، با شرکتهای دیگر آشنا شوند، وضعیت صنعت را بهتر ببینند و درباره همکاریهای احتمالی صحبت کنند. به گفته بنیانگذار دوات، این ارتباطها میتوانند به همکاریهایی برای یکپارچهسازی محصولات و خدمات منجر شوند؛ اتفاقی که بدون شبکهسازی و حضور همزمان بازیگران صنعت بهسادگی رخ نمیدهد. یکی از ارتباطهایی که در الکامپ شکل گرفت نیز حتی بعد از نمایشگاه ادامه پیدا کرد و به گفته او، یکی از طرفین همچنان پیگیر ادامه همکاری بود. اما خود صنعت دیگر شبیه گذشته نیست مساله اینجاست که حتی همین امکان شبکهسازی هم زمانی ارزشمندتر است که تعداد و تنوع کسبوکارهای حاضر در نمایشگاه، تصویری واقعی از صنعت ارائه دهد. بنیانگذار دوات میگوید تصویر او از الکامپ پیش از حضور، با واقعیتی که در نمایشگاه دید تفاوت داشت. چیزی که بیش از همه توجه او را جلب کرد، کاهش شور و حال و فعالیت در فضای استارتاپی بود؛ وضعیتی که آن را بیارتباط با مشکلات چند سال اخیر کشور و کاهش انگیزه جوانان نمیداند. به این ترتیب، الکامپ با یک تناقض روبهرو شده است. از یک طرف هنوز میتواند آدمها و کسبوکارهایی را کنار هم قرار دهد که خارج از نمایشگاه شاید یکدیگر را پیدا نکنند؛ از طرف دیگر، همان صنعتی که قرار است در نمایشگاه خود را به نمایش بگذارد، در بیرون از نمایشگاه با محدودیتها و اختلالهایی مواجه است که مستقیما بر ادامه فعالیتش اثر میگذارد. دوات نمونه این وضعیت است. کسبوکاری که در الکامپ ۲۸ برای معرفی محصول و پیدا کردن ارتباط تجاری حاضر شده بود، چند ماه بعد به دلیل قطعی اینترنت مجبور شد سرورها را خاموش کند و بنیانگذاران شرکت نیز برای دسترسی به اینترنت از ایران خارج شدند. البته امسال اوضاع بدتر از دوره قبل هم شده بود. در دوره گذشته، شرکتهای متنوعی از سراسر کشور در این بخش حاضر بودند و راهکارهای مختلفی را که با هدف حل مسائل کسبوکارها و با محوریت هوش مصنوعی توسعه داده بودند، ارائه میکردند. اما امسال، در کنار برخی محصولات و راهکارهای کاربردی، بخش قابل توجهی از غرفهها به سرویسهایی اختصاص داشت که بیشتر در لایه استفاده از مدلهای آماده قرار میگرفتند؛ از پشتیبانی فروش هوشمند گرفته تا دسترسی به API سرویسهایی مانند ChatGPT، Gemini و Claude و فروش اشتراک برای استفاده از آنها. این مشاهده بهتنهایی نمیتواند درباره کل بازار هوش مصنوعی ایران حکم صادر کند، اما دستکم در ویترین الکامپ میتوان تفاوت را شاهد بود. اگر قرار است الکامپ تصویری از وضعیت صنعت فناوری ایران ارائه کند، تغییر جنس چنین غرفههایی میتواند پرسش مهمی ایجاد کند. آیا بازار در حال بلوغ و حرکت به سمت محصولات قابل استفاده است یا هنوز بخش بزرگی از آن در مرحله سوار شدن بر ابزارها و مدلهایی است که جای دیگری توسعه داده شدهاند؟ الکامپ چهار روزه تمام نمیشود با این حال، از نگاه مدیران دوات، ارزش نمایشگاه را نباید با انتظار برای یک نتیجه فوری سنجید. برکت مومنی معتقد است نمایشگاه بهخودیخود بازار بزرگی برای یک کسبوکار نمیسازد. ممکن است ارتباطی در نمایشگاه ایجاد شود و یک سال بعد به مشتری یا همکاری تبدیل شود؛ آنقدر دیر که حتی شرکت بهسادگی نتواند تشخیص دهد این رابطه از کدام نمایشگاه آغاز شده است. در چنین مدلی، بخش مهمی از ارزش نمایشگاه بعد از پایان چهار روز آن مشخص میشود. شرکت باید ارتباطهایی را که در نمایشگاه ایجاد کرده پیگیری کند؛ موضوعی که به گفته بنیانگذار دوات، بسیاری از شرکتها انجام نمیدهند و در عین حال انتظار دارند صرفاً با حضور در نمایشگاه مشتری یا سرمایهگذار پیدا کنند.
impact: افزایش انگیزه مهاجرت بنیان‌گذاران و کند شدن روند نوآوری در اکوسیستم فناوری ایران.
