title_en: کمیسر حقوق بشر سازمان ملل: هوش مصنوعی می‌تواند خطری وجودی برای بشریت باشد
summary: کمیسر عالی حقوق بشر سازمان ملل خواستار تعیین خطوط قرمز بین‌المللی برای جلوگیری از خطرات هوش مصنوعی پیشرفته شد.
او از تمرکز قدرت نامحدود در دست چند شرکت محدود مانند اوپن‌ای‌آی، متا و آنتروپیک ابراز نگرانی کرد.
تأکید اصلی سازمان ملل بر ایجاد سازوکارهای نظارتی مستقل و بررسی تأثیر AI بر شغل‌ها، محیط‌زیست و دموکراسی است.
full_text: کمیسر حقوق بشر سازمان ملل: هوش مصنوعی میتواند خطری وجودی برای بشریت باشد کمیسر عالی حقوق بشر سازمان ملل با اعلام هشدار درباره خطرات هوش مصنوعی پیشرفته، خواستار تعیین خطوط قرمز بینالمللی برای قابلیتهای این فناوری شد. «فولکر تورک»، کمیسر عالی حقوق بشر سازمان ملل متحد، با هشدار درباره خطرات احتمالی هوش مصنوعی پیشرفته برای بشریت، از کشورهایی که میزبان توسعه این فناوری یا در زنجیره تأمین آن هستند خواست درباره تعیین خطوط قرمز بینالمللی برای قابلیتهایی که هوش مصنوعی نباید هرگز به آنها دست پیدا کند، توافق کنند. تورک این اظهارات را در جریان ارائه گزارش جهانی خود به شورای حقوق بشر سازمان ملل در شصتوسومین نشست این شورا در ژنو مطرح کرد. او تهدیدهای ناشی از فناوریهای جدید برای حقوق بشر را «ناآشنا و حتی بیسابقه» توصیف کرد و گفت: «من نگرانیهای افراد فعال در صنعت را درباره اینکه هوش مصنوعی پیشرفته میتواند خطری وجودی برای بشریت ایجاد کند، درک میکنم و با آنها همنظر هستم.» او درباره وضعیت حکمرانی هوش مصنوعی نیز گفت: «نیاز به حکمرانی بر هوش مصنوعی بهطور گسترده پذیرفته شده است، اما اقدام کجاست؟» نظرات کمیسر سازمان ملل درباره هوش مصنوعی کمیسر عالی حقوق بشر سازمان ملل علاوه بر دولتها، به تمرکز قدرت در صنعت هوش مصنوعی نیز اشاره کرد و گفت: «تعداد انگشتشماری از مردان تقریباً قدرت نامحدودی بر هوش مصنوعی دارند.» او در این زمینه نام شرکتهایی از جمله آنتروپیک، متا و اوپنایآی را مطرح کرد و گفت دفتر او قصد دارد با این شرکتها وارد تعامل شود و همه مسائل را صرفاً از مسیر دولتها دنبال نکند. تورک همچنین درباره سطح توانایی سیستمهای هوش مصنوعی که باید غیرقابلقبول تلقی شود، معیارهایی مشخص مطرح کرد. او گفت: «هوش مصنوعی که از محیط آزمایش خود فرار کند یا برای جلوگیری از خاموششدن خود، از توسعهدهندگان باج بگیرد، بیشازحد قدرتمند است.» تورک علاوهبر تعیین خطوط قرمز، خواستار تضمینهای قوی برای ایمنی و امنیت هوش مصنوعی و ایجاد سازوکارهای راستیآزمایی مستقل شد؛ سازوکارهایی که به گزارشدهی خود شرکتها متکی نباشند. او همچنین خواستار ارزیابی تأثیرات هوش مصنوعی بر اشتغال، دموکراسی و محیط زیست شد. ایده تعیین خطوط قرمز بینالمللی برای هوش مصنوعی پیشازاین نیز مطرح شده است. فراخوان جهانی برای خطوط قرمز هوش مصنوعی (Global Call for AI Red Lines) که در سپتامبر ۲۰۲۵ در مجمع عمومی سازمان ملل متحد راهاندازی شد، با حمایت بیش از ۲۰۰ نفر، از جمله ۱۰ برنده جایزه نوبل، خواستار آن شده بود که دولتها تا پایان سال ۲۰۲۶ درباره محدودیتهای الزامآور به توافق برسند و نهادی مستقل مسئول اجرای آن باشد. سازمان ملل متحد پیشتر نیز درباره فاصله میان سرعت پیشرفت هوش مصنوعی و توانایی نظامهای حکمرانی برای مدیریت آن هشدار داده بود. در ژوئیه، دبیرکل سازمان ملل در گفتوگوهای جهانی درباره حکمرانی هوش مصنوعی در ژنو موضعی مشابه را مطرح کرده بود.
impact: افزایش فشار سیاسی بر غول‌های فناوری برای پذیرش چارچوب‌های الزام‌آور بین‌المللی.

title_fa: جذب سرمایه ۳ میلیارد یورویی میسترال؛ غول هوش مصنوعی اروپا ارزش‌گذاری شد
title_en: Mistral Raises €3B Series D to Expand Sovereign AI
summary: میسترال در دور جدید جذب سرمایه، ۳ میلیارد یورو دریافت کرد تا ارزش این استارتاپ فرانسوی از ۲۱ میلیارد یورو بگذرد.
سامسونگ در کنار صندوق‌های بزرگ اروپایی رهبری این سرمایه‌گذاری را برعهده دارد تا استقلال فناوری اروپا در برابر آمریکا حفظ شود.
هدف اصلی میسترال از این تامین مالی، توسعه زیرساخت‌های پردازشی و بزرگ‌تر کردن مدل‌های هوش مصنوعی بومی است.
full_text: Mistral announced on September 8, 2026 that it has raised €3 billion in a Series D funding round at a post-money valuation of more than €21 billion, which the company said is the largest equity fundraising round ever completed by a European technology company, three years after its launch. Samsung Electronics led the round, joined by co-leads Scaleup Europe Fund, which is managed by EQT, and existing investor PSG Equity. Investors in the Round Advent, funds and accounts managed by BlackRock, and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg joined the round as new investors. Existing investors a16z, ASML, Belfius, BNP Paribas CIB, Bpifrance, Carmignac, DST Global, Eurazeo, General Catalyst, Headline, Hillspire, Index Ventures, Korelya Capital, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Phoenix Court’s Solar fund (home to LocalGlobe, Latitude and Solar) and Salesforce Ventures also participated. Mistral said the round reflects a strategic endorsement from investors across Europe, Asia and North America, bringing together a syndicate of strategic and financial investors that includes global technology leaders, growth investors and existing shareholders that have supported its development to date. With a Series C led by ASML and the Series D now led by Samsung Electronics, the company said it has attracted backing from companies at the forefront of advanced manufacturing, engineering and industrial technology, adding that this support reflects growing confidence that its approach can help organizations deploy state-of-the-art AI inside complex real-world environments while maintaining control over their data, infrastructure and knowledge. Co-lead Scaleup Europe Fund is a European Union initiative structured as a multi-billion late-stage and growth fund targeting strategic technology companies, with artificial intelligence named among its focus areas. According to the European Innovation Council, the fund is anchored by a €1 billion European Commission commitment alongside founding investors including Novo Holdings, EIFO, CriteriaCaixa, Santander/Mouro Capital, Allianz and Wallenberg Investments, and EQT was selected as its fund manager through a competitive public call. The fund was set to make its first investments in autumn 2026. Stated Use of Proceeds Mistral said the round will significantly expand its frontier research, which it described as the foundation underpinning its infrastructure, products and sovereignty. The company said the funding will allow it to scale its compute capacity for training powerful models and will help it expand infrastructure and accelerate its commercial growth and international footprint. The company said it now operates across 20 countries and supports the mission-critical AI transformation of more than 125 global enterprises, naming Airbus, ASML and HSBC among them. The Company’s Sovereign AI Positioning In the announcement, Mistral framed the round around a shift it sees in how organizations approach AI. During the first wave of generative AI, the company said, the central question was who could build the most powerful model; organizations and governments are now asking how to harness AI for mission-critical needs without surrendering control over the infrastructure and intelligence loop. The company said demand for that combination of performance with control, choice and independence is growing internationally as enterprises and governments weigh the long-term technology dependencies, data governance requirements and deployment choices that come with any AI investment. Mistral described itself as the only AI company in the world building what it called the full stack required to answer that question: open-weight models, the infrastructure and compute capacity they run on, and the products that bring them into production, ensuring customers are never locked into a single vendor’s roadmap, pricing or availability. The company said its full-stack and open approach allows organizations to build on it without exposing their most valuable data, workflows and institutional knowledge to anyone outside their own walls. Mistral said this is what makes its stack the sovereign AI layer, which it defines as retaining control across four dimensions: data that stays inside the organization’s boundaries, models that are controllable and customizable, compute that is private and predictable, and systems in production that are fully controllable and auditable. Prior Funding and Company Timeline Mistral’s previous round was a €1.7 billion Series C at an €11.7 billion post-money valuation, announced on September 9, 2025 and led by semiconductor equipment manufacturer ASML, with participation from existing investors DST Global, Andreessen Horowitz, Bpifrance, General Catalyst, Index Ventures, Lightspeed and NVIDIA. According to the company’s own timeline, Mistral was founded in April 2023, hired its first employee in June 2023 and raised a seed round that same month, followed by a Series A in December 2023 and a Series B in June 2024. The company lists co-founders Arthur Mensch as CEO, Guillaume Lample as Chief Science Officer and Timothée Lacroix as CTO.
impact: تثبیت موقعیت اروپا در رقابت جهانی هوش مصنوعی و کاهش وابستگی به غول‌های فناوری آمریکایی.

title_fa: کشف خطای اندازه‌گیری که طراحان باتری را گمراه می‌کرد
title_en: Bumpy battery surfaces can masquerade as nanoscale ion pathways, misleading material design
summary: محققان KAIST دریافتند ناهواری‌های سطحی در مقیاس نانو سیگنال‌هایی شبیه به حرکت یون‌ها ایجاد می‌کنند و باعث تحلیل اشتباه عملکرد باتری می‌شوند.
با روش جدید حذف این سیگنال‌های کاذب، مسیر ساخت باتری‌های حالت جامد و سدیمی بسیار دقیق‌تر و سریع‌تر می‌شود.
full_text: Bumpy battery surfaces can masquerade as nanoscale ion pathways, misleading material design A signal that appears to show ions moving inside a battery may, in fact, be an illusion caused by an uneven surface. A KAIST research team has identified the origin of this type of artifact, which can lead researchers to misinterpret what is happening inside a battery, and has developed a method to reduce it. The findings are expected to enable more accurate analysis of ion movement and improve the reliability of next-generation battery-material development, including that of solid-state and sodium-ion batteries. A research team led by professor Seungbum Hong from the Department of Materials Science and Engineering, in collaboration with the research groups of professor Jong Min Yuk from the same department and professor Nam-Soon Choi from the Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, has identified the cause of a measurement artifact in nanoscale battery analysis that can be mistaken for actual ion transport. The team also proposed a method for effectively reducing this artifact. The paper is published in the journal Small Methods. During charging and discharging, lithium or sodium ions move back and forth within a battery. The speed and ease with which these ions move affect the battery's performance and lifespan. Developing better batteries therefore requires researchers to precisely determine where ions can move freely and where their movement is hindered. Testing the false signal One technique used for this type of analysis is electrochemical strain microscopy (ESM), which is based on atomic force microscopy (AFM). ESM scans the surface of a battery material with an extremely fine tip and measures nanoscale changes in the material associated with ion movement, allowing researchers to indirectly track ion transport. The problem is that when the surface of a battery material is rough, similar signals can appear even in the absence of actual ion movement. If these signals are interpreted as evidence of ion transport, researchers may incorrectly identify where ions are moving within the material. To investigate the origin of these artifacts, the team created fine trenches on the surface of an ionically inactive single-crystal silicon sample. This provided an experimental environment in which no ions were moving while the sample surface remained uneven. The results quantitatively demonstrated that variations in surface height alone can alter the degree of contact between the microscope tip and the sample, producing signals similar to those generated by actual ion movement. The same phenomenon was also observed in actual battery materials. When the team analyzed a graphite anode and the sodium solid electrolyte Na₂Zn₂TeO₆, the ESM signals likewise varied according to surface topography. This confirmed that the issue is not limited to a particular material but is a phenomenon that researchers must account for when conducting nanoscale analyses of a wide range of battery materials. Smoothing away the artifact As a solution, the team proposed making the surfaces of battery materials as smooth and flat as possible. To achieve this, the researchers used a cooling cross-section polisher (CCP), which employs an argon (Ar) ion beam to precisely polish sample cross sections. Because argon is chemically inert under most conditions, this technique allows the surface to be processed precisely without significantly altering the properties of the sample. This treatment substantially reduced surface roughness and, in turn, decreased measurement artifacts caused by uneven surfaces. The mechanism is comparable to a car moving up and down while traveling over a bumpy road: As the scanning tip passes over height variations on the surface of a battery material, the degree of contact between the tip and the sample changes. These changes can generate signals resembling those produced by actual ion movement. In particular, the team examined signals detected at grain boundaries—the interfaces where the small crystals that make up a battery material meet, much like the seams between adjacent tiles. Before the surface was smoothed, strong ESM signals appeared at these grain boundaries. After the surface was polished, however, the enhanced signals disappeared. This finding indicates that some signals previously interpreted as evidence of "pathways that facilitate ion transport" may actually have resulted from variations in surface height rather than genuine ion movement. Better data for battery design This study is significant because it experimentally demonstrates how this type of measurement artifact arises in nanoscale battery analysis and shows that it can be reduced using the practical approach of smoothing battery-material surfaces. The findings are expected to provide a more accurate understanding of where ions move freely and where their movement is hindered within a battery. Such insights could provide an important foundation for designing battery materials that facilitate ion transport, thereby enabling faster charging and longer battery life. The team expects this analytical approach to be applicable not only to widely used lithium-ion batteries but also to next-generation battery systems. These include solid-state batteries, which use solid rather than liquid electrolytes, and sodium-ion batteries, which use sodium ions in place of lithium ions. The approach could help researchers more accurately understand how these batteries operate and support the design of new materials. Furthermore, the accumulation of reliable nanoscale analysis data could provide high-quality training data sets for artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning research aimed at designing new battery materials and predicting their performance. title_en: Huawei Mate XT 2 Ultimate Tri-Fold Smartphone Launched with Kirin 9050 Pro SoC, HarmonyOS 7, 5600mAh Battery
summary: نسل جدید گوشی تاشوی سه‌تکه هواوی با نمایشگر ۱۰.۲ اینچی و پردازنده قدرتمند Kirin 9050 Pro معرفی شد.
این پرچمدار ۲۸۰۰ دلاری به سیستم‌عامل HarmonyOS 7، قابلیت اجرای همزمان سه برنامه و ارتباط ماهواره‌ای مجهز است.
full_text: Huawei Mate XT 2 Ultimate Tri-Fold Smartphone Launched with Kirin 9050 Pro SoC, HarmonyOS 7, 5600mAh Battery Huawei has unveiled the Mate XT 2 Ultimate Design in China, pushing the boundaries of foldable smartphone technology with a massive 10.2-inch tri-fold display. The successor to Huawei's earlier tri-fold device can transform from a compact smartphone into a tablet-sized screen and packs flagship hardware, satellite connectivity and an advanced camera system. The Huawei Mate XT 2 Ultimate Design is positioned firmly in the ultra-premium segment, with prices starting at 19,999 yuan (roughly Rs. 2.81 lakh). Huawei Mate XT 2 Gets a 10.2-Inch Tri-Fold Display The biggest highlight of the Mate XT 2 Ultimate is its G-shaped tri-fold design, allowing users to switch between single-screen, dual-screen and full tablet modes. When folded, it offers a 6.5-inch OLED display, while the fully unfolded device features a 10.2-inch flexible OLED panel. The inner display offers a 2232 x 3184 pixel resolution, a 1Hz to 90Hz LTPO refresh rate and 1440Hz PWM dimming. Meanwhile, the outer screen supports a 120Hz LTPO refresh rate and up to 6,500 nits of peak brightness. Huawei says the phone measures 12.3mm when folded and just 3.5mm at its thinnest point when opened. Despite its complex design, the device weighs 299g. It also gets IP58 and IP59 ratings for dust and water resistance. Kirin 9050 Pro Powers the Tri-Fold Flagship Under the hood, the Mate XT 2 Ultimate is powered by Huawei's Kirin 9050 Pro chipset, paired with 16GB of RAM and up to 2TB of storage. Huawei claims significant CPU performance improvements over the previous generation. The phone runs HarmonyOS 7, which is optimised for the larger display with support for three apps running side by side, split-screen multitasking and desktop-class PC applications. Huawei has also included a graphene vapour chamber cooling system and an upgraded GPU with support for advanced graphics features, including real-time ray tracing. 50MP Cameras, Satellite Features and Privacy Screen The Huawei Mate XT 2 Ultimate features a 50MP RYYB main camera with OIS and a variable aperture, alongside a 40MP ultra-wide lens and a 50MP periscope telephoto camera offering 3.5x optical zoom. Connectivity options include 5G, NFC, Wi-Fi 802.11ax, Bluetooth 6.0, USB Type-C and satellite communication features. The phone supports Tiantong satellite calls and two-way BeiDou satellite messaging. Huawei is also offering a special privacy screen edition featuring hardware-level technology designed to reduce visibility from side angles. The Mate XT 2 Ultimate packs a 5,600mAh battery with 66W wired and 50W wireless charging. It also supports the M-Pen 3 stylus. Huawei Mate XT 2 Ultimate Design prices go up to 29,999 yuan for the top-end Special Edition. The phone goes on sale in China from September 7, while India availability is yet to be announced.

title_fa: کاهش ۱۰۰ برابری مصرف انرژی دیتاسنترهای AI با پالس‌های مغناطیسی
title_en: Scientists say ‘ultrafast magnetic-field pulses’ could help AI data centers cut ...
summary: محققان دانشگاه ادینبرو روش جدیدی کشف کرده‌اند که با استفاده از پالس‌های فوق‌سریع میدان مغناطیسی، حالت حافظه RAM را تغییر می‌دهد.
این تکنیک مصرف برق حافظه‌ها در دیتاسنترهای سنگین هوش مصنوعی را تا ۱۰۰ برابر کاهش می‌دهد و بحران انرژی AI را مهار می‌کند.
full_text: When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission. AI data centers currently use a huge amount of energy Scientists have found a way to cut that energy bill by "orders of magnitude" It involves using "ultrafast magnetic-field pulses" in RAM and storage It's no secret that the current artificial intelligence (AI) boom is leading to record levels of energy consumption — all that computing power needs to be fueled somehow — and it's causing much controversy among the communities that are impacted whenever a new data center lays down its roots in their neighborhoods. Now, though, scientists think they've come across a way that could radically slash the energy requirements of memory and storage, with potentially massive consequences for the future of the computing and AI industries. In a paper published in the Advanced Materials journal (via a press release in Science Daily), researchers at the University of Edinburgh in Scotland wrote that the breakthrough would fundamentally affect the way magnetic memory operates. Right now, switching its state allows magnetic memory to control digital information, but the current methods of doing so can be costly in terms of energy. Instead of using standard energy switching techniques, the researchers discovered an alternative that harnessed ultrafast magnetic field pulses that consumed far less energy. In fact, the paper claimed that the authors' approach could cut energy usage by "up to two orders of magnitude" — in other words, a cut of around 100x, which is a significant reduction. The data centers of the future The AI revolution is only a few years old, but data center energy consumption has already become a significant issue. As the authors of the research paper put it, "Without significant improvements in efficiency, [information and communication technologies] could eventually represent a sizable share of worldwide electricity consumption and carbon emissions." AI is playing a large role in that trend thanks to both its voracious appetite for component production and the sizable emissions it produces. While the paper focused on magnetic memory, its theories could be applied to other fields, the authors believe. As study writer Dr. Elton J.G. Santos put it, "The same framework can be adapted to electrical currents and even ultrafast laser pulses, which are among the most cutting-edge technologies for future data storage. That means the ideas developed here could have applications far beyond the systems we studied." Although the research is still in the realm of theory, the paper's authors proposed a number of practical steps that could help others build prototypes and conduct experiments. That said, don't expect monumental changes any time soon. There is still a long road ahead before these ideas get put into practice, if they ever do. But given the promising results of the scientists' work, there is hope that the data centers of the future could be far less energy-intensive than those of today.

summary: جشنواره تلوراید مستند جدیدی درباره ۳۴ روز پایانی آزادی الیزابت هولمز پیش از ورود به زندان ۱۱ ساله را به‌طور کاملاً محرمانه اکران کرد.
این فیلم توسط کمپانی A24 در ماه اکتبر عرضه می‌شود و دسترسی بی‌سابقه‌ای به زندگی خصوصی بنیان‌گذار ترانوس داشته است.
full_text: Telluride just managed one of its best-kept secrets in years, per The Hollywood Reporter. On Sunday night, festivalgoers filed into a 650-seat theater with their phones locked away, having no idea what they were about to see, told only that it ran nearly three hours, hadn’t been shown anywhere, and that its principal creators would be in the audience. The surprise premiere they went on to enjoy is a new documentary from co-directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes. Called “You Can See Everything,” the film is said to capture Holmes and her husband, Billy Evans, in the 34 days before she reported to federal prison in May 2023 to begin an 11-year sentence for defrauding investors about her blood-testing technology. Since then, her legal fight has limped along without success. Her appeals to overturn the conviction and shorten her sentence were rejected in February of last year. She then went a different route last year, asking President Trump to commute her sentence. That clemency petition is still listed as pending, meaning it’s officially been opened and remains under review. Fielder apparently lived in the couple’s guest house during filming — the access they provided sounds shocking — but some of the buzz also ties to an A-list actress who becomes part of the story itself. A24 is set to release the film in October. You can check out the trailer below.

title_fa: مدیرعامل آرم: هوش مصنوعی درمان سرطان را پیدا می‌کند، اگر تراشه داشته باشیم
title_en: مدیرعامل آرم: هوش مصنوعی در طول زندگی ما سرطان را درمان خواهد کرد
summary: رنه هاس معقتد است هوش مصنوعی به‌زودی معمای پیچیده درمان سرطان را حل می‌کند، اما کمبود شدید تراشه مانع اصلی است.
او تأکید کرد تا زمانی که ده‌ها میلیارد دلار صرف ساخت کارخانه‌های تراشه‌سازی جدید نشود، ظرفیت پردازشی به درمان بیماری‌ها نمی‌رسد.
به گفته هاس، توسعه داتاسنترهای چندگیگاواتی و تجهیزات پیشرفته شرط اصلی جهش فناوری در حوزه سلامت و رباتیک است.
full_text: مدیرعامل آرم: هوش مصنوعی در طول زندگی ما سرطان را درمان خواهد کرد به گفته مدیرعامل آرم، کمبود شدید تراشه و نیاز به مراکز داده بزرگ، بزرگترین موانع پیشرفت هوش مصنوعی و حل معماهای پزشکی هستند. مدیرعامل بزرگترین شرکت فناوری بریتانیا، یعنی Arm، معتقد است که هوش مصنوعی در طول عمر نسل حاضر به راهکاری برای درمان بیماری سرطان دست پیدا خواهد کرد که از عهده تواناییهای انسان خارج است. اما ابتدا باید مشکل گلوگاه محاسباتی را حل کنیم. «رنه هاس»، مدیرعامل شرکت طراح تراشه آرم هولدینگز (Arm Holdings) مستقر در کمبریج، اعلام کرده ساخت یک مدل از نحوه تأثیرپذیری نشانگرهای ژنتیکی سرطان درحالحاضر مسئلهای بیشازحد پیچیده محسوب میشود، اما رایانهها در آینده این معضل بزرگ را برطرف خواهند کرد. هاس که از فوریه ۲۰۲۲ سکان هدایت این مجموعه را در دست دارد و پیش از آن نیز هفت سال به عنوان نایبرئیس بخش محصولات پردازشی در انویدیا فعالیت کرده میگوید: «من همیشه فکر میکردم که برگ برنده و کاربرد حیاتی هوش مصنوعی در حوزه سلامت است. هوش مصنوعی نهتنها مدتزمان لازم برای ابداع داروها را کوتاهتر میکند، بلکه زمان آزمایش آنها را نیز بهشدت کاهش خواهد داد. من معتقدم در طول دوران زندگی ما، هوش مصنوعی به درمان سرطان کمک خواهد کرد.» بااینحال، رسیدن به چنین نقطهای از نظر او مستلزم ظرفیت پردازشی فوقالعاده بالایی است. به گفته هاس، تراشههایی که میتوانند برای تحقیقات پزشکی، درمان سرطان و همچنین توسعه رباتهای انساننما در پنج سال آینده استفاده شوند، توسط شرکتهای هوش مصنوعی که درحال طراحی مراکز داده با ظرفیت چندین گیگاوات هستند، مصرف میشوند. او دراینباره به برنامههای ساخت مراکز داده بسیار بزرگ چند گیگاواتی در فرانسه و آمریکا و حتی طرحهای ارسال آنها به مدار زمین اشاره کرد و گفت جهان در شرایط محدودیت جدی عرضه قرار دارد و حتی پیش از فرستادن مراکز داده به فضا، به کارخانههای ساخت تراشه بسیار بیشتری نیاز است. همچنین ساخت این کارخانهها راهحلی فوری به حساب نمیآید، چراکه تأسیس هر کدام دهها میلیارد دلار هزینه دارد و دو تا سه سال زمان میبرد. هاس میگوید: «درحالحاضر شرایط بهشدت محدود است. فقط این را بگویم که پیش از آنکه بتوانیم یک مرکز داده را در فضا مستقر کنیم، به کارخانههای تراشهسازی بیشتری نیاز داریم. احتمالاً زمانی مراکز داده را به فضا میفرستیم که بزرگترین مانع مراکز داده، هزینه خود مرکز داده باشد.» هوش مصنوعی و حل معمای پیچیده سرطان حتی بدون در نظر گرفتن کمبود تراشه، تضمین درمان سرطان با هوش مصنوعی در سالهای پیش رو کار آسانی نخواهد بود. پژوهشگران حوزه سلامت یادآوری میکنند که سرطان یک بیماری واحد نیست، بلکه مجموعهای متشکل از بیش از ۱۰۰ نوع بیماری مختلف محسوب میشود که علائم و ساختار متفاوتی در بدن هر بیمار دارند. هرچند هوش مصنوعی به پژوهشگران امکان میدهد اهداف سلولی را شناسایی و رفتار احتمالی داروها را پیشبینی کنند، شواهد موجود پیرامون اثربخشی بالینی آن همچنان محدود است و متغیرهای بیشمار درون بدن مدلسازی قطعی اثر دارو روی انسان را دشوار میکنند. در سوی دیگر، پروفسور «کریس باکال» از مؤسسه تحقیقات سرطان لندن و مدیرعامل شرکت Sentinal4D، معتقد است چالش واقعی دیگر بر سر استفاده از هوش مصنوعی نیست، بلکه مسئله اصلی خوراک و دادههایی است که در اختیار آن قرار میگیرد. به گفته او، تیمهای آزمایشگاهی درحال آموزش هوش مصنوعی با دادههای تولیدشده از نمونههای بیماران هستند که از اینترنت جمعآوری نشده و نیازی هم به راهاندازی مراکز داده غولپیکر ندارد. او تأکید کرده آینده هوش مصنوعی پزشکی در اختیار کسانی نخواهد بود که بزرگترین کامپیوترها را میسازند، بلکه متعلق به مجموعههایی است که دقیقترین اندازهگیریها را در اختیار دارند. درهمینحال، توسعه بیرویه مراکز داده در آمریکا، که شمار آنها تا پایان سال گذشته از مرز ۱۴۰۰ مورد عبور کرده، چالشهای محیط زیستی متعددی به بار آورده؛ تا جایی که یک نظرسنجی نشان میدهد هفت نفر از هر ۱۰ شهروند بزرگسال آمریکایی با احداث مراکز داده هوش مصنوعی در نواحی زندگی خود به دلیل پیامدهای منفی بر آبوهوا مخالف هستند.
impact: ضرورت سرمایه‌گذاری سنگین زیرساختی در صنعت نیمه‌هادی برای تحقق وعده‌های پزشکی هوش مصنوعی.

summary: اپل قصد دارد بالاخره وارد بازار گوشی‌های تاشو شود؛ مدلی موسوم به «آیفون اولترا» که قیمتی بالای ۲۰۰۰ دلار خواهد داشت.
این دستگاه در حالت بازشده نمایشگر ۷.۸ اینچی ارائه می‌دهد و برای کاهش ضخامت، حسگر Face ID جای خود را به Touch ID روی کلید جانبی داده است.

full_text: It’s finally happening — this week, we are (probably) about to see Apple’s first foldable iPhone, more than five years after Samsung launched its first foldable phone. Apple’s annual iPhone release events are always interesting in one way or another, but this year’s presentation is one of the most anticipated in a while. As Tim Cook hands off the CEO role to former Vice President of Hardware Engineering John Ternus, people have high expectations for Apple’s next devices, especially since the company is embracing an entirely new form factor. While Apple is usually tight-lipped about its product launches, there are always inevitable leaks, giving us insight into what we might see during the September 9 Apple event. While the foldable iPhone is most exciting, we’re also anticipating news about AirPods, HomePods, and the non-foldable iPhone 18 line. What we think we know so far about the foldable “iPhone Ultra” If Apple has made its consumers wait over half a decade for it to enter the foldable market, its first attempt had better be good — especially since reports indicate that the phone will cost more than $2,000. At least it’s not as pricey as the $3,500 Apple Vision Pro headset, and unlike headsets, people actually buy smartphones. The good news is that people who claim to be early testers of the device have reported back positive experiences. According to Bloomberg’s Apple insider Mark Gurman, the foldable iPhone has a premium feel, fits nicely into a pocket, and opens up into a wide, iPad-like display. The phone is expected to sport a 5.5″ cover display, which expands to 7.8″ when the screen is unfolded. When folded in, the device will look shorter and wider than a typical iPhone. To make hardware that’s still sleek enough to pocket when folded, Apple has had to make some concessions. The device reportedly skips the telephoto camera, which could be disappointing to the kind of consumers who are willing to open their pockets for a phone that’s expensive enough to feed a family for months. However, the phone is expected to have a dual-lens rear camera system with a main and an ultra-wide lens, similar to what’s on Apple’s more basic iPhones. Rumor has it that Apple will include MagSafe, the magnetic wireless charging and accessory system, but that it will forego Face ID to save space, relying instead on a Touch ID fingerprint button on the phone’s side. This shouldn’t be a huge concession — touching a button is about as easy as looking at a screen — but it might take some getting used to if you’ve become accustomed to Face ID. Like other foldable phones, the iPhone Ultra is expected to support side-by-side multitasking, letting you run two apps at once, one on each half of the unfolded screen. Even though it’ll resemble a small iPad when opened up, it will still run iOS rather than iPadOS, though shouldn’t be cause for concern, since Apple’s newest chips are powerful enough to handle it. In fact, the same chip reportedly powers Apple’s budget MacBook Neo laptop. A pain point for foldable phone users thus far has been the dreaded “crease.” With other companies’ foldable phones, you can see the evidence when you open the phone that this isn’t your standard display. It’s a hard problem to solve and one that maybe isn’t worth the technical effort, though Apple has supposedly created a display where the crease isn’t as visible. Don’t worry, you can still get a new iPhone that doesn’t fold If foldables aren’t your thing — or if you don’t want to spend double the price on your next phone — don’t worry. Apple is also expected to release some new devices in the iPhone 18 line. We’ve heard leaks about the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, but not much yet about the standard iPhone 18, which is predicted to arrive six months after the September event. That would be a first for Apple — releasing the premium models before the standard one. Siri HomePods? AirPods with cameras? Now that Apple is finally moving forward with its Gemini-powered Siri AI update, the company is also expected to refresh the HomePod, a smart speaker and Apple’s answer to devices like the Amazon Echo line. References to unreleased products, including new HomePods, were recently spotted by users digging through a macOS preview build. The most surprising find, however, is that Apple appears to be working on AirPods with built-in cameras. In that same macOS preview, researcher Aaron Perris found a video showing someone wearing the AirPods and picking up a book. “With Visual Intelligence, your world becomes savable. See something you like? Just ask me to save it for later,” a voiceover in the video says. While some users may be skittish about using a device that can see what they see — comparisons to Meta’s maligned “pervert glasses” are inevitable — we have some degree of hope that a company like Apple, which has built its brand on privacy, will do better. Gurman has reported that “the cameras essentially act as eyes for the Siri digital assistant and aren’t designed to take photos or video.” Instead, the earbuds’ components allow it to “capture visual information in low resolution.”

title_fa: کاهش سن بیولوژیک انسان با داروی هوش مصنوعی اینسیلیکو
title_en: AI-designed drug candidate reverses biological age in clinical study
summary: شرکت اینسیلیکو با ترکیب هوش مصنوعی مولد و تحلیل‌های پروتئومیکس، داروی rentosertib را توسعه داده که سن بیولوژیکی بیماران را عقب کشیده است.
آزمایش بالینی فاز دوم نشان می‌دهد این دارو علاوه بر معکوس‌کردن سن سلولی، عملکرد ریه بیماران مبتلا به فیبروز ریوی را به شکل معنی‌داری بهبود می‌دهد.
این نخستین‌بار است که یک داروی کاملاً طراحی‌شده با AI (و نه یک داروی قدیمی تغییرکاربری‌یافته) در فاز بالینی چنین نتایجی ثبت می‌کند.
full_text: Insilico Medicine ("Insilico"), a clinical-stage company focused on generative AI-driven drug discovery and development, today announced the publication of a new study conducted in collaboration with an international team of scientists from Harvard Medical School, Stanford University, The Broad Institute, RWTH Aachen University, Peking University and Westlake University. Using longitudinal Olink proteomic data (CNCB OMIX accession: OMIX008341) collected during a Phase IIa clinical trial of rentosertib, researchers evaluated biological age using six internationally recognized, independently developed proteomic aging clocks. All six models consistently indicated a reduction in predicted biological age among patients treated with rentosertib. In addition, the Forced Vital Capacity (FVC), the essential measure of lung function declining with age, showed promising dose-dependent reversal compared to placebo aligning with the proteomic aging clock age reversal. Recently published in Nature Biotechnology, the study represents the first clinical evaluation of a potentially first-in-class drug candidate featuring both an AI-discovered target with relevance to aging and disease biology and an AI-designed molecule, rather than a repurposed generic drug such as rapamycin or metformin. The findings also provide a proof-of-concept framework for integrating aging biomarkers into standard clinical trials to accelerate the discovery of geroprotective drugs and longevity therapeutics. The results will be presented by first author Alex Zhavoronkov, founder and CEO of Insilico Medicine, at the Nature conference: Redefining Healthcare in the Age of AI, to be held at Sorbonne University in Paris on September 8, 2026. From aging biology to a clinical drug Unlike traditional geroscience studies that rely on repurposed drugs like rapamycin or metformin, Insilico pursued a different approach by incorporating aging biology into its drug discovery strategy from the outset. Using its AI-powered target discovery platform, Insilico identified TNIK as a novel target implicated in aging and fibrosis and performed hallmarks of aging assessment where TNIK scored highly in 6 hallmarks. TNIK was subsequently prioritized as a dual-purpose target relevant to both underlying aging biology and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Insilico's generative chemistry platform, Chemistry42, was then deployed to design the small-molecule candidate rentosertib targeting TNIK. The program progressed from target identification to preclinical candidate nomination in approximately 18 months, with the preclinical findings published in Nature Biotechnology in 2024. In June 2025, Insilico reported the results of a Phase IIa trial of Rentosertib for IPF (NCT05938920) in Nature Medicine. The trial met its primary safety endpoint and demonstrated a promising dose-dependent trend in efficacy. One of the common efficacy outcome measures is Forced Vital Capacity (FVC), the essential measure of lung function. The typical age of onset of IPF is around 65 years. Interestingly, in healthy individuals older than 65, FVC declines as well typically at the rate of 20-50 mL/year and may also serve as a potential physiological biomarker of aging. In the previous publication, it was revealed that in the 60-mg once-daily group, patients experienced a mean improvement in forced vital capacity (FVC) of +98.4 mL, compared with a mean decline of -20.3 mL in the placebo group (-62.3 excluding outlier). Crucially, the trial protocol prospectively included longitudinal serum proteomic screening for exploratory biomarker analyses, which proved consistent with the drug's proposed anti-fibrotic and anti-inflammatory activity. All data collected from the trial were subsequently deposited with the China National Center for Bioinformation (CNCB), enabling the current investigation of biological aging biomarkers. Six different clocks point to strong biological age reversal measured by proteomics In the current study, researchers evaluated serum proteome profiles from 42 trial participants across 2,841 proteins. The team applied six independently developed proteomic aging clocks, including ProtAge, OrganAge (chronological and mortality variants), PAC, ipfP3GPT, and PAOPAC. Despite relying on diverse methodologies and training criteria, all six clocks consistently exhibited a trend toward reversed biological age among rentosertib-treated patients compared to placebo. The peak effect is observed at Week 4 in participants receiving 30 mg BID with approximately 3-4 years reversal in biological age and up to 6 years in a certain aging clock. Rentosertib decreases predicted biological age across various regimens as measured by most aging clocks, most significantly in the 30 mg BID group and in week 4. Beyond changes in biological age scores, the study showed that rentosertib's anti-aging effects operate partially independent of its respiratory benefits. Notably, the dose associated with the greatest improvement in lung function differed from that producing the strongest age-reversal signal, suggesting that the drug's geroprotective activity was not merely a downstream consequence of disease improvement. This systemic impact was further validated through comparisons with 55,319 UK Biobank profiles, which showed that rentosertib directly reversed the typical age-related protein-expression trajectories. Mechanistically, the drug acted as a senomorphic agent, suppressing key drivers of cellular senescence, including EREG, ESM1, IGFBP4, ITGA2, MMP10, MMP13, and SPP1 while downregulating growth-factor signaling pathways associated with accelerated aging, including RTK-PI3K and RAS-ERK, and modulating antioxidant and cholesterol metabolisms. A framework for the future To support reproducibility and further research, all research data have been deposited at CNCB (accession OMIX008341), and the underlying pipeline code has been published as the open-source Python library on GitHub. full_text: From Pixxel’s $100 million Series C to Nua’s $50 million round, and Paytm’s Vijay Shekhar Sharma predicting AI agents will replace apps by 2027, YourStory brings you today's headlines and the latest news across sectors. Spacetech startup Pixxel raised $100 million in a Series C led by Temasek and Seraphim, taking total funding to $195 million. The company said it will expand its Honeybee constellation and high resolution optical satellites, build the Aurora software platform and scale production through its Gigapixxel facility. Women’s wellness brand Nua raised $50 million in a Series C led by Peak XV and Filter Capital, with participation from Mirabilis Investment Trust and Footpath Ventures. The round includes primary and secondaries, and Nua said it will invest in brand building, distribution expansion and R&D. Paytm founder Vijay Shekhar Sharma predicted that autonomous AI agents will replace smartphone apps by 2027. In a post on X, he said OS level access will let personal agents execute multi step tasks and forecast 2026 would cement machines’ lead in code generation. Navana.ai, a sovereign voice AI company serving regulated enterprises, has raised Rs 40 crore in a Series A funding round led by entrepreneur and investor Ronnie Screwvala. The round also saw participation from Sharad Sanghi, Antler India, Sandeep Singhal and Paula Mariwala. The Bengaluru-based company will use the fresh capital to scale its deployments across the BFSI sector, expand its speech models for Indian languages and dialects, and accelerate product development for its AI Contact Centre and automated evaluation platform. Pet food brand Lickicious has raised Rs 19 crore in growth capital through a mix of equity and institutional debt as it looks to scale its business and achieve Rs 100 crore in annual revenue. The funding round was led by Prath Ventures, with participation from the founders of Atomberg and several industry executives. The company said it will use the capital to expand manufacturing capacity, strengthen research and development, and broaden its product portfolio. Swiggy has launched a 24x7 helpline and a dedicated ‘Food Safety’ section in its app to allow customers to report food safety concerns related to their orders. The in-app option allows users to provide details and upload photographs. Customers who report concerns through the helpline will receive a link on their registered mobile number to submit additional information and images. Swiggy said complaints submitted through either channel will be reviewed by its Food Safety Assurance Team, which will take further action based on the issue. Kochi-based healthcare technology company Cyrix Healthcare, backed by private equity firm Somerset Indus Capital Partners Fund III, has acquired the MedTech Solutions business of Blue Star Engineering & Electronics (Blue Star E&E). The acquisition will expand Cyrix’s medical imaging capabilities, particularly in CT and MRI, as well as its services across equipment sales, installation, maintenance, repairs and refurbishment. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

title_fa: ممنوعیت هوش مصنوعی در مدارس؛ راهکار یا فرار از مسئله؟
title_en: Ban on Students' AI Use and the Bigger Problem Facing Us All
summary: ممنوع‌کردن ابزارهای AI در دانشکده‌ها و مدارس چالش اصلی یعنی آموزش تفکر انتقادی و خلاقانه به دانش‌آموزان را حل نمی‌کند.
سیستم‌های آموزشی باید به‌جای حذف هوش مصنوعی، بازتعریف کنند چه بخش‌هایی از تفکر باید در ذهن فرد بماند و چه بخش‌هایی به ابزارها واگذار شود.
full_text: Ban on Students' AI Use and the Bigger Problem Facing Us All Research shows disruptive innovations are declining. How can schools reverse it? Posted September 7, 2026 Reviewed by Jessica Schrader Key points - To ban or not to ban: AI technology allows us to re-delegate what students will do mentally vs. externally. - To develop students' critical, creative, strategic, and ethical thinking, consider which tasks can use AI. - As knowledge expands beyond human limits, future innovators need to know how to use AI well. New York City just hit pause on students' use of AI. Will other districts follow suit? And should they? The answer may impact all of us far into the future, as I explain below. Perhaps we can all agree on the main question: What do we want to see in the next generation? Individually, productive citizens with fulfilling lives. Collectively, a better world than what we left them. But that is a tall order, as the world they inherit has huge, seemingly intractable problems like climate change. We expect them to tackle these problems with technology. What Is Technology? "Technology" is now synonymous with "computing." At one point, the wheel, pen, and paper were new technologies. Technology is simply an invention that expands our capacity to do things. Writing as a technology overcame human limits on memory. Plato voiced reservations about moving from orality to literacy. The ability to recite at length was lost, rendered superfluous when everything was captured permanently on paper for perusal into posterity. The oral practice of preserving collective knowledge through dialogue morphed into manuscripts and libraries. In doing so, the collective minds of a Socratic circle multiplied a million-fold. Internal Mental Resources vs. External Capacity In placing the current debate on AI in context, consider what internal mental resources we want to preserve and nurture in our young. And what external tools and technology we want them to be equipped to use. We want them to be able to think in ways that can stand up to the challenges that they will inevitably encounter. The key word is "think." Critical, creative, strategic, and ethical thinking are all essential in ensuring that the next generation can weather the storms to come—and thrive. If we break each type of thinking into its task components, the question becomes clearer: Which part do we want our children to develop internally and which can we safely relegate to external supports? For each type of thinking, a table below illustrates examples of tasks that may be relegated to AI or the student. Critical Thinking - Skeptical examination of carefully selected valid information to arrive at sound judgment. We could try to suppress students’ use of AI to do these tasks. Or we could allow them to do so but demand more. For example, ask them to justify why they picked certain options and discarded others. Creative Thinking - Identifying problems, seeing new patterns, connecting disparate domains, and exploring solutions in situations with no right answers. In a fluid, fast-changing environment, thinking outside the box is critical, as the world needs more inventors and problem-solvers. Strategic Thinking - Understanding the situation, identifying goals, crafting a feasible solution to achieve these goals, and anticipating opportunities and threats. For workers, entrepreneurs, and corporations, strategic thinking is a survival skill. Ethical Thinking - Considerations of harm to others, society, and self. Moral development should be embedded in our children's education, not just a course module. The question in education is not just about AI use. The problem in education is in not getting students to practice all four thinking skills widely. Where Were We Pre-AI? Consider what the public school system was like before 2023, the watershed year for public use of AI. Poor literacy and math achievement was already endemic: barely one-third of students were proficient in national assessments (NAEP, 2023). Claims of causation demand valid evidence from causal studies. There are many possible culprits to rule out first: the pandemic, fewer families eating dinner together, less bedtime reading, the rise in children's screen time, and the rise in parents' screen time. What Is AI? Generative AI is not all there is to AI. AI is a collection of technologies that simulate human intelligence by performing tasks traditionally done by humans. Some forms of AI surpass human expertise in certain tasks due to the advantages of computing. By the same token, humans excel in other tasks over AI. So the trick is in getting the best of human ability and AI. Challenge 1: 70% Not Proficient The majority of students in the U.S. are not proficient in literacy and math. In this case, human capacity is simply insufficient to resolve the problem. Reading difficulty is primarily due to inefficiencies in processing language in the brain. This problem may require AI to overcome human limitations of capacity and speed (May & Van Horne, 2025). Challenge 2: 30% Not Creative Of the students who are proficient in reading and math, much is asked of them, given the societal problems they inherit. Humankind faces challenges that require big breakthroughs. We need disruptive innovators, yet they are less likely in the future (Park et al., 2023). What Is Disruptive Innovation and Why Is It Declining? As an inventor with software patents in AI, let me present it this way: An innovation has novelty. A patented invention is also non-obvious to even practitioners in that field. A disruptive innovation is novel, non-obvious, and revolutionary. Such breaks from the past combine disparate domains together in unexpected ways. This is creative thinking. The exponential expansion of knowledge forces scientists to work in narrow slices, making potent connections across fields less likely. Schools need to train scientists-to-be to use technology to surmount this limit. More than just rethinking

title_fa: آموزش غول جدید OpenAI با بیش از ۱۰۰ هزار کارت گرافیک انویدیا
title_en: آموزش مدل هوش مصنوعی GPT-6 Astra با بیش از ۱۰۰ هزار پردازنده گرافیکی انویدیا
summary: مدل جدید GPT-6 Astra با بیش از ۱۰۰ هزار پردازنده گرافیکی Grace Blackwell انویدیا آموزش دیده و قرار است این ظرفیت به ۴۰۰ هزار کارت برسد.
مدیران OpenAI مدعی شده‌اند که این مدل مرزهای هوش عمومی مصنوعی (AGI) را رد کرده و بخش عظیمی از توان محاسباتی آن صرف ایمنی و همراستایی شده است.
دسترسی آزمایشی به GPT-6 Astra برای برخی سازمان‌ها آغاز شده و به‌زودی در دسترس عموم قرار می‌گیرد.
full_text: جنسن هوانگ، مدیرعامل انویدیا، اعلام کرد مدل جدید OpenAI با نام GPT-6 Astra با استفاده از بیش از ۱۰۰ هزار پردازنده گرافیکی از نوع Grace Blackwell NVLink72 آموزش دیده است. به گفته او، برنامههایی برای فعالسازی ۴۰۰ هزار پردازنده گرافیکی دیگر نیز در دست اجرا قرار دارد. بهگزارش پیسی گیمر، دسترسی به GPT-6 Astra از اوایل هفته جاری برای تعداد محدودی از سازمانها آغاز شده و قرار است بهزودی برای کاربران عادی نیز فراهم شود. گرگ براکمن، یکی از بنیانگذاران و رئیس OpenAI، این آموزش را نخستین اجرایی دانست که روی بیش از ۱۰۰ هزار پردازنده گرافیکی انجام شده است. براکمن در گفتوگو با Stratechery گفت: «این نخستین باری بود که روی بیش از ۱۰۰ هزار پردازنده گرافیکی آموزش دادیم.» او درباره مفهوم هوش جامع مصنوعی یا AGI نیز اظهار داشت: «مردم تعریف خودشان را از AGI دارند؛ تقریبا چیزی مبهم است. شاید مدل قبلی بود، شاید Astra، شاید مدل بعدی، اما جایی در این میان، فکر میکنم از آستانه AGI بیشتر مردم عبور خواهیم کرد.» هوانگ در شبکه اجتماعی X مدعی شده «AGI فرا رسیده است». این ادعا در حالی مطرح میشود که OpenAI اعلام کرده GPT-6 Astra در چندین معیار ارزیابی هوش مصنوعی از جمله FrontierMath Tier 4، ARC-AGI 3 و TerminalBench-4.0 عملکردی پیشرفته دارد. براکمن تأکید کرد بخش بزرگی از توان محاسباتی این مدل صرف ایمنی و همراستایی شده است. او گفت: «بخش زیادی از توان محاسباتی Astra صرف ایمنی و همراستایی میشود و کار امنیتی گستردهای پیرامون آن انجام شده است. فکر میکنم حجم عظیمی از کار برای ارائه امن این مدل انجام دادهایم.» زمانبندی این ادعاها با گمانهزنیها درباره عرضه اولیه سهام OpenAI همزمان شده است. همچنین معرفی Astra تنها چند هفته پس از آن رخ داد که یک «جمع عاملها» از محیط ایزوله آزمایشی OpenAI خارج شد و به سرورهای Hugging Face حمله کرد. نظر شما درباره ادعای رسیدن به AGI و هزینه سختافزاری عظیم مدلهای جدید هوش مصنوعی چیست؟ دیدگاه خود را با ما در میان بگذارید.
impact: جهش تاریخی در قدرت محاسباتی هوش مصنوعی و نزدیک‌تر شدن واقعی به هوش عمومی مصنوعی (AGI).

این ورک‌استیشن با پشتیبانی از ۵۷۶ گیگابایت حافظه HBM3e و پهنای باند ۱۶ ترابایت بر ثانیه، اجرای محلی غول‌پیکرترین مدل‌های هوش مصنوعی را ممکن می‌کند.
full_text: AMD در نمایشگاه IFA قدرتمندترین راهکارهای خود برای توسعهدهندگان و کاربران حرفهای هوش مصنوعی را به نمایش گذاشت؛ از Threadripper Halo Station گرفته تا مجموعهای از کامپیوترهای مجهز به Ryzen AI MAX که اجرای مدلهای هوش مصنوعی بهصورت محلی را هدف قرار دادهاند. Threadripper Halo Station در برابر NVIDIA DGX Station؛ قدرتمندترین قابلیتهای هوش مصنوعی در یک کامپیوتر دسکتاپ تقاضا برای اجرای سریع هوش مصنوعی بهصورت محلی بهشدت در حال افزایش است. با بزرگتر شدن مدلها و محبوبیت روزافزون ایجنتهای هوش مصنوعی، نیاز به سختافزار قدرتمند نیز با سرعت زیادی افزایش پیدا کرده است. این نیاز به راهکارهایی با قدرت پردازشی بالا منجر شده تا AMD قدرتمندترین سیستم هوش مصنوعی خود تا امروز را معرفی کند: Threadripper Halo Station. ایامدی Threadripper Halo Station صرفاً یک ورکاستیشن معمولی مجهز به تردریپر نیست. این سیستم بهترین سختافزارهای رده PRO AMD را در یک دستگاه جمع کرده و ایامدی آن را «Ultimate Personal AI Workstation» یا «قدرتمندترین ورکاستیشن شخصی هوش مصنوعی» مینامد. در بخش مشخصات، AMD Threadripper Halo Station از سریعترین پردازندههای تردریپر این شرکت، مانند Threadripper PRO 9995WX، استفاده میکند. این پردازنده حداکثر ۹۶ هسته Zen 5 و در مجموع ۱۹۲ رشته پردازشی دارد، فرکانس آن به حداکثر ۵.۴ گیگاهرتز میرسد و به ۳۸۴ مگابایت حافظه کش مجهز شده است. این یعنی قدرت پردازشی بسیار زیادی در اختیار کاربران قرار میگیرد. یک پردازنده سریع برای اجرای فرایندهای هوش مصنوعی عاملمحور ضروری است، اما GPUها نیز اهمیت بسیار زیادی دارند. برای پاسخ به نیازهای پردازشی هوش مصنوعی، این سیستم از دو GPU ورکاستیشن AMD Instinct استفاده میکند. این کارتها جدیدترین مدلهای MI350P هستند که هرکدام به ۱۴۴ گیگابایت حافظه HBM3e مجهز شدهاند. این سیستم در نهایت میتواند حداکثر چهار کارت از این نوع را در خود جای دهد و به رقم بسیار بزرگ ۵۷۶ گیگابایت حافظه HBM3e برسد. مجموع پهنای باند حافظه این GPUها نیز میتواند به ۱۶ ترابایتبرثانیه برسد. علاوهبراین، سیستم از مقدار زیادی حافظه استاندارد DDR5 از نوع RDIMM نیز پشتیبانی میکند. Threadripper Halo Station میتواند تا ۲ ترابایت حافظه RDIMM داشته باشد که در نتیجه مجموع حافظه سیستم را به ۲.۶ ترابایت و مجموع پهنای باند حافظه را به ۱۶.۴ ترابایتبرثانیه میرساند. در این ترکیب، حافظه HBM وظیفه ارائه پهنای باند بالا را برعهده دارد، درحالیکه حافظه RDIMM ظرفیت بیشتری را در اختیار سیستم قرار میدهد. کل سیستم از طراحی خنککننده مایع بهره میبرد و در یک شاسی استاندارد E-ATX قرار گرفته است. لوگوی AMD در قسمت جلویی دستگاه دیده میشود و طراحی ظاهری آن نیز از زبان طراحی Halo استفاده میکند که AMD پیشتر در مینیپیسیهای Ryzen AI Halo خود به کار گرفته بود. نتیجه این ترکیب، امکان صرفهجویی قابلتوجه در هزینه اجرای هوش مصنوعی است؛ چراکه کاربران میتوانند مدلهای AI را بهصورت محلی اجرا کنند و به جای پرداخت مبالغ بالا برای اشتراک سرویسهای هوش مصنوعی ابری، پردازشها را روی سیستم خود انجام دهند. تردریپر Halo Station قادر خواهد بود مدلهایی با تریلیونها پارامتر را اجرا کند و عرضه آن برای سال ۲۰۲۷ برنامهریزی شده است. یکی از مزایای راهکار AMD این است که از قطعاتی استفاده میکند که بهراحتی قابل تهیه و جایگزینی هستند. بنابراین کاربران میتوانند قطعات داخلی سیستم را بر اساس نیازهای خود با یکدیگر ترکیب یا در آینده تعویض کنند. طبیعتاً باید بررسی کنیم این سیستم در برابر رقیب خود چه عملکردی دارد. ایامدی Threadripper Halo Station مستقیماً در برابر انویدیا DGX Station قرار میگیرد. در مقایسه Threadripper Halo Station و DGX Station، راهکار AMD در بخش پردازنده مرکزی از تعداد هستهها و رشتههای بیشتری برخوردار است. معماری Zen 5 بهرهوری بسیار خوبی دارد و از نظر IPC نیز عملکرد قدرتمندی ارائه میدهد؛ بنابراین عملکرد تکهستهای بالاتری را شاهد خواهیم بود و با وجود ۱۹۲ رشته، عملکرد چندهستهای نیز بسیار سریع خواهد بود. در بخش حافظه، تراشه GB300 انویدیا بهصورت منفرد حافظه HBM بیشتری دارد، اما AMD با استفاده از چهار شتابدهنده میتواند مجموع حافظه HBM3e را به ۵۷۶ گیگابایت برساند. انویدیا همچنین امکان ارتقای قابلیتهای سیستم با استفاده از کارتهای AIC اختصاصی را در اختیار کاربران قرار میدهد. برای مثال، کارت پرچمدار 96 GB RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell میتواند ۱۹۲ گیگابایت حافظه دیگر به سیستم اضافه کند. این حافظه از نوع GDDR7 است که از نظر پهنای باند نسبت به حافظه HBM3e در MI350P AMD سرعت پایینتری دارد. از طرف دیگر، GPUهای Instinct ظرفیت حافظه ۵۰ درصد بیشتری نیز ارائه میدهند. در مجموع، حجم حافظه قابل استفاده در راهکار ایامدی از انویدیا بیشتر است. قیمت تردریپر Halo Station همچنان مشخص نشده است، اما AMD سابقه ارائه محصولات خود با قیمتهای رقابتی را دارد. DGX Station با قیمتی نزدیک به ۱۰۰ هزار دلار عرضه میشود؛ بنابراین انتظار میرود ایامدی قیمت سیستم خود را در همین محدوده تعیین کند یا آن را با قیمت پایینتری به بازار بفرستد. البته ایامدی لزوماً مجبور نیست قیمت پایینتری تعیین کند، چراکه راهکار این شرکت مزایای قابلتوجهی دارد. Ryzen AI MAX 400؛ اجرای حداکثری هوش مصنوعی محلی در کامپیوترهای قابل حمل در کنار Threadripper Halo Station، ایامدی و شرکا در نمایشگاه IFA مجموعه قدرتمندی از کامپیوترهای مجهز به Ryzen AI MAX 400 را نیز به نمایش گذاشتند. اعلامیههای کامل AMD در نمایشگاه IFA به شرح زیر است: - سیستمهای AMD Ryzen AI Halo بهصورت پیشفرض از Project Zenith مایکروسافت پشتیبانی خواهند کرد. این قابلیت تجربه جدیدی از ویندوز برای توسعهدهندگان ارائه میدهد که برای دستگاههای پرقدرت بهینه شده است. این سیستمها بهصورت پیشفرض با Visual Studio Code ،WSL، گیتهاب کوپایلوت CLI و PowerShell عرضه میشوند تا فرایند توسعه هوش مصنوعی بهصورت محلی سادهتر شود. - AMD Threadripper Halo Station یک نمونه اولیه است که قابلیت پردازش هوش مصنوعی در سطح دیتاسنتر را به ورکاستیشنهای دسکتاپ میآورد. این سیستم با ترکیب Ryzen Threadripper PRO 9995WX و دو شتابدهنده رده Instinct، به توسعهدهندگان اجازه میدهد مدلهای عظیم هوش مصنوعی را بدون وابستگی به محدودیتهای سرویسهای ابری، بهصورت محلی آموزش دهند، Fine-tune کنند و اجرا نمایند. - AMD و SUSE نیز از همکاری خود برای کمک به توسعهدهندگان خبر دادهاند. هدف این همکاری، انتقال اپلیکیشنهای هوش مصنوعی از مرحله توسعه و آزمایش محلی روی AMD Ryzen AI Halo به محیطهای تولیدی سازمانی امن و پشتیبانیشده در مقیاس بزرگ است. AMD همچنین بخشی از قابلیتهای عملکردی نسل بعدی سیستم Ryzen AI Halo را با تراشه Ryzen AI MAX+ 495 و حداکثر ۱۹۲ گیگابایت حافظه یکپارچه به نمایش گذاشت. این سیستم توانست مدل GLM-5.3 Flash با ۳۲۰ میلیارد پارامتر را بهصورت محلی اجرا کند و به سرعت ۵۸ توکن بر ثانیه (TPS) دست پیدا کند. این عملکرد قابلتوجه است؛ چراکه برای استفا
impact: بی‌نیازی توسعه‌دهندگان از سرورهای ابری گران‌قیمت با انتقال قدرت پردازش AI به کامپیوترهای شخصی.

title_fa: ورود ربات‌های انسان‌نما از استیج رقص به میدان نبرد چین
title_en: From dance floor to war: China readies humanoid robots for combat
summary: ارتش چین در حال انتقال سریع تکنولوژی ربات‌های انسان‌نما از آزمایشگاه‌ها به میدان‌های تمرین نظامی است.
سرمایه‌گذاری سنگین چین روی استفاده از ربات‌ها به عنوان «رزمنده» جهت اجرای عملیات در محیط‌های پرخطر صورت می‌گیرد.
تسلط ۹۵ درصدی شرکت‌های چینی بر بازار جهانی ربات‌های انسان‌نما، دسترسی بی‌نظیری به ارتش این کشور داده است.
full_text: By Eduardo Baptista BEIJING, Sept 7 (Reuters) - At the World Humanoid Robot Games in China last month, robots jumped, boxed and danced. Some fleet-footed bots ran faster than Usain Bolt over 100 meters. Spectators cheered the machines' improving capabilities and their meme-worthy stumbles. Two days after the Games ended, the People's Liberation Army's official newspaper drew its own conclusions from the show. The PLA Daily called for researchers to accelerate the transfer of cutting-edge technologies from laboratories to military training grounds for robotic "combatants." China's defense establishment is accelerating research into humanoids' military uses and planning for their eventual wartime deployment, according to a Reuters review of more than 100 Chinese military procurement notices, academic studies, patents, official publications, government records and defense-company materials. Military institutions are testing humanoids against battlefield requirements, seeking to acquire robots and technologies to train them, and studying how they might function alongside troops, the previously unreported records show. The work gained momentum in 2025 and 2026, focusing on robot perception, manipulation, and training data. Chinese manufacturers accounted for about 95% of global humanoid shipments in 2025, according to BofA Global Research. That commercial dominance gives the PLA access to an expanding industry while developing its own military applications. China's robot defense research underscores how rapidly military technologies are evolving globally. In the Russia-Ukraine war, semiautonomous drones that use artificial intelligence for navigation and targeting have transformed reconnaissance and attack, while robots carry supplies and retrieve casualties. Reuters has previously documented the Chinese military's efforts to learn from Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II. That evolution is driving worldwide military interest in autonomous systems. "Going where we don't want humans to go is one of the most compelling reasons to develop robots in the first place," said Dennis Hong, a professor of mechanical and aerospace engineering at UCLA. "If losing a robot means avoiding the loss of a human life, then the robot can become expendable." China's defense ministry and the National University of Defense Technology (NUDT), the PLA's premier research institution, didn't respond to requests for comment about humanoid robots' military applications. Reuters found no evidence that China has deployed an armed humanoid with an operational PLA unit. The robots remain energy-intensive and unreliable outside controlled demonstrations. Battlefield environments pose many variables and challenge robots' abilities in unpredictable ways, said Aaron Johnson, a professor of mechanical engineering at Carnegie Mellon University. URBAN ASSAULT FORCE Already, China has a vision for humanoid robots in urban warfare. Six "combat robots" – humanoids, robot dogs or unmanned vehicles – would be split up between two assault teams. Working with ground troops, the robots would clear an enemy-occupied building, floor-by-floor and room-by-room. That scenario was described in an August 2025 paper by researchers at NUDT's test center in Xi'an. The study modeled an urban assault force using equipment the authors projected could be available within five to 10 years. It didn't specify the robots' rules of engagement, the weapons they would carry, nor how they would handle civilian encounters. Improvements in balance, perception and endurance could make humanoids useful in places including buildings, tunnels and ship interiors, said Juo-Min Chou, a researcher at Taiwan's Institute for National Defense and Security Research. "Their two hands and two feet could, in theory, combine mobility, climbing and manipulation," she said. For simpler reconnaissance or logistics missions, however, quadruped, tracked or wheeled robots would generally be cheaper and easier to deploy at scale, Chou added. Chinese military commentary envisions an expanding range of roles for humanoids. A July 2025 article in PLA Daily argued that humanoid missions could eventually evolve "from supporting combat toward primary combat" and discussed how robots might be authorized to fire on a living target that had been verified by a human. In December, the PLA Eastern Theater Command released an AI-generated montage that showed military robots, including humanoids and quadrupeds, overwhelming Taiwan's defenses in a hypothetical future conflict. China isn't alone in exploring battlefield uses for humanoids. Last year, the U.S. Army launched a competition to develop "militarized humanoid capabilities" that could eventually work alongside soldiers. The Army said potential roles included reconnaissance, security, obstacle clearing, hazardous-material operations and offensive and defensive missions in urban terrain. Up to 10 finalists were due to test their systems with U.S. military experts this year, with as much as $1.25 million available for follow-on contracts. The U.S. robotics industry, however, trails far behind China in developing two-legged and four-legged machines. Reuters reported last month that China's Unitree robots – among the world's leading producers of humanoids and quadrupeds – based designs for its best-selling robot dogs on innovations financed by the U.S. military. The Pentagon and the U.S. Army didn't comment for this story. INFILTRATING ENEMY LINES Chinese interest in humanoid robots' military applications began to pick up in 2024. That year, NUDT and China's Academy of Military Sciences hosted a defense-technology forum that included a session on military applications for humanoid systems, according to NUDT's website. Neither institution responded to Reuters' questions. A year later, NUDT explicitly framed humanoid robots as battlefield tools. title_fa: معرفی گوشی فوق باریک تکنو CAMON Slim 5G
title_en: The CAMON Slim 5G is TECNO's latest ultra-slim smartphone
summary: تکنو گوشی باریک ۶.۳۹ میلی‌متری خود را با تراشه دایمنسیتی 7300e و پشتیبانی از 5G به‌روزرسانی کرد.
این دستگاه با وجود ضخامت کم، به باتری ۶۰۰۰ میلی‌آمپری و گواهی سرسختانه IP69K مجهز است.
full_text: TECNOhas been focused on making super-slender smartphones for the masses. Their first “Slim” phones made their debut with theSPARK and POVA series. This time, it has also arrived towards the CAMON line. TheTECNO CAMON Slimwas announced not too long ago.ICYMI,it’s rocking a MediaTek Helio G200 Ultimate SoC. That also meant that this phone is limited to 4G. That’s about to change with the newerTECNO CAMON Slim 5G. Despite the sameslim chassis at 6.39mm, they changed the core toMediaTek’s Dimensity 7300e chipset. This enables faster 5G speeds in a more powerful octa-core processor. Definitely, the battery of the CAMON Slim 5G isquite bigger at 6000mAhover the 5600mAh. Albeit, charging speed isslower at 45Wversus 60W of its 4G counterpart. Utmost durability was also given importance with itsquadruple IP66, IP68, IP69, and IP69K water and dust resistance ratings. It has passed military-grade MIL-810-STD certifications as well as a TÜV SÜD certification for 60 months of sustained fluidity. The changes don’t end just with internals alone. While both share the same6.78-inch 1.5K 144Hz AMOLED screen, the CAMON Slim 5G possesses aflat displayover the curved ones of the regular CAMON Slim. Other display feats remain such as TÜV Rheinland’s low blue light certification, as well as Rain Touch, Waterproof Case Touch, and even Wet & Oily Hand Touch Recognition 2.0 Rain Touch that boosts touch sensitivity even under watery conditions. Flipping to the back, you’ll see the biggest change. The fun-looking camera bar with its AI Mood Light was removed in favor of a vertical-styled camera placement together with the iconic swan-neck curve design like the rest of the CAMON 50 line.
impact: تحول در طراحی گوشی‌های باریک با حفظ ظرفیت باتری و مقاومت بالا.

title_en: Lenovo Unveils ThinkCentre Desktops, ThinkBook Laptops, ThinkVision Monitors And New Concepts At IFA 2026
summary: لنوو از کیس‌های تجاری ThinkCentre X Ultra با پشتیبانی از پردازنده‌های رایزن AI Max+ پرده برداشت.

full_text: Lenovo has unveiled its latest commercial portfolio at Lenovo Innovation World during IFA 2026, covering desktop PCs, laptops, monitors and two proof-of-concept devices – including one that introduces fan-less active cooling into laptops courtesy of Frore Systems. ThinkCentre X Ultra & ThinkCentre M75 Series The ThinkCentre X Ultra is a compact 1.6L desktop powered by up to AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 processor with up to 128GB of unified memory. It integrates with the AMD Ryzen AI Developer Center for access to preconfigured AI tools and models across Windows and Linux. A cluster-ready architecture allows up to four units to be connected for expanded compute and memory resources, supporting larger AI models and multi-agent workflows. The ThinkCentre M75s Gen 6 is a small form factor desktop with up to AMD Ryzen AI PRO 400 Series processors, while the ThinkCentre M75q Gen 6 is a compact tiny desktop supporting up to 64GB of memory and up to four simultaneous displays, designed for flexible placement including monitor mounting and desk drawer installation. Both include self-healing BIOS and ThinkShield security as standard. ThinkBook 14 Gen 9 & ThinkBook 14x Gen 2 The ThinkBook 14 Gen 9 is powered by Snapdragon X2 Plus processors in a 17.7mm-thin, 1.3kg chassis, featuring Lenovo Qira with features including Pay Attention and Catch Me Up for meeting assistance, along with optional touch support and up to 26 hours of local video playback. The ThinkBook 14x Gen 2 is an ultra-thin option at 12.9mm and 990g, powered by Intel Core 7 Series 3 processors, with OLED display options, optional LCD touch, and color choices including Luna Grey, Celestial White, Mystic Violet and Veil Blue. New ThinkVision Monitors The ThinkVision P34WD-4v is a 34-inch WQHD curved 21:9 monitor, which Lenovo claims as the world’s first Thunderbolt VoIP monitor certified by Microsoft Teams. It includes a 5MP camera with automatic face framing, multi-participant detection, distance-based volume adjustment and Windows Hello sign-in; it also features an adaptive refresh rate between 24Hz and 120Hz, alongside smart sensors for brightness adjustment, privacy detection and automatic dimming. The ThinkVision P27UL-40 is a 27-inch 4K OLED monitor using InkJet Printing technology for improved color accuracy, contrast and efficiency. It covers 99% DCI-P3 and 100% sRGB, carries VESA DisplayHDR True Black 500 certification, and includes TÜV Rheinland Eye Comfort 5-star certification with circadian-friendly display adjustments reducing harmful blue light to 20% or below. Synchronized brightness controls and a mirrored power button are also integrated with compatible Lenovo laptops. The ThinkVision T32UD-4v (31.5-inch UHD) and T34WD-4v (34-inch 21:9) round out the monitor announcements, both carrying Microsoft Teams certification, Windows Hello, USB-C docking with up to 100W power delivery and a 48-120Hz variable refresh rate. Two New Lenovo Concepts The first of the two concepts is referred as Project AeroBlade: this is a 14-inch concept laptop measuring under 10mm thick, which is the level of thickness that almost wouldn’t fit conventional cooling fans. Lenovo teamed up with Frore Systems – best known for its AirJet solid-state active cooling modules – to develop its “Active Flow” thermal solution that is still capable of producing active airflow through vibrating membranes; the chassis uses magnesium-aluminum construction to achieve 830g weight as well. Project Swan, meanwhile, is a concept that functions as a 14-inch laptop in compact mode and expands to a 17-inch 16:9 display in roll-out mode for wider multitasking, side-by-side document work and presentations; wimilar implementations have been found in the likes of Legion Pro Rollable, ThinkPad Rollable XD, and the ThinkBook Plus Gen 6 Rollable (which you could buy). It measures 17.9mm thin at 1.6kg, which is no bulkier than a conventional equivalent. Pokdepinion: Took it long enough for Frore’s cooling systems into laptops proper.

summary: استارتاپ هندی Pixxel با حمایت گوگل و هدایت نماسک، ۱۰۰ میلیون دلار سرمایه جدید جذب کرد.

full_text: INDIAN space tech startup Pixxel said on Monday it had raised $100 million in a Series C funding round led by Singapore state investor Temasek and British space-technology venture firm Seraphim, marking the single-largest funding round by a space technology company in India. Google-backed Pixxel’s latest round included existing investors Radical Ventures and growX Ventures, as well as new investors 360 ONE Asset and IMM Investment, bringing its total funding to $195 million, the company said. Pixxel is one of the Indian space startups that emerged after the government opened the sector to private players. Founded by Awais Ahmed, Pixxel began with hyperspectral satellites that could reveal information about the Earth’s surface beyond what conventional imagery could capture. Since then, it has expanded its scope to include Aurora, its Earth intelligence software, and satellite systems for both commercial and sovereign space missions. Together, these form the core of Pixxel’s planetary infrastructure vision, connecting sensors, software, and space systems to help governments, industries, and institutions turn Earth observation into actionable intelligence, its statement said. The fresh capital will help Pixxel expand its sensing capabilities through its Honeybee satellite constellation and high-resolution optical imaging satellites, while further developing Aurora as a platform that combines these datasets into decision-ready insights.

title_fa: پدیده انتخاب بیش‌ازحد؛ چطور الگوریتم‌ها خلاقیت را یک‌دست می‌کنند؟
title_en: How 'hyperselection' is making modern life efficient, pleasant
summary: الگوریتم‌های بهینه‌سازی در پلتفرم‌ها باعث تکرار فرمول‌های موفق قبلی و حذف ایده‌های ریسکی شده‌اند.
این روند یک‌دست‌سازی در حوزه‌های مختلف از موسیقی و فوتبال تا پژوهش‌های دانشگاهی به چشم می‌خورد.
full_text: It’s difficult to imagine a song like Queen’s 1975 Bohemian Rhapsody topping the charts today. Almost six minutes long, it moves through several radically different musical sections and famously ignores the conventional structure of a pop song. It seems almost designed to break the rules of what a hit single should be. Fifty years later, popular music seems to have moved in the opposite direction. Once artists and producers figure out what makes a commercial hit – from its length and structure to its rhythm, melody and how quickly it reaches a catchy hook – songs can be optimised to reproduce them. This tendency is especially pronounced today because streaming platforms allow millions of songs to compete for our attention. This creates intense pressure to stick to formulas that are known to work rather than risk experimenting with something different. As a result, the musical landscape becomes filled with songs that sound alike. This is an example of what my colleagues and I call hyperselection in a new paper published in the journal Frontiers in Psychology. This idea refers to what happens when competition becomes so intense, and we become so adept at identifying and optimising what succeeds, that we repeatedly select for the same characteristics while alternatives are eliminated. When we become too good at figuring out what works Beyond music, hyperselection is making many parts of our world more efficient and optimised while simultaneously making them more predictable, mediocre and sterile. In professional football, teams constantly search for tactics that give them an advantage. Once a strategy proves successful, other teams follow suit. The game becomes increasingly competitive and tactically sophisticated, but teams also become all the more similar in how they play while leaving less room for individual flair. The same happens in academia. Scientists are rewarded for publishing papers, receiving citations and attracting research funding. These are reasonable indicators of scientific performance. But intense competition can encourage researchers to pursue studies that are easier to conduct and more likely to be published, rather than risky ideas that might fail but could also produce important breakthroughs. Urban settings provide another example. Shops, restaurants and developments that are commercially successful are copied and reproduced, while those that cannot compete disappear. Cities thousands of kilometres apart can therefore become filled with the same Starbucks, Apple stores and luxury malls. Variety is valuable One consequence of hyperselection is the loss of adaptive variance. This refers to the variability that comes from allowing different products, behaviours and strategies to coexist, including those that may not be the most efficient. This matters for more than whether our music, cities or football matches become boring. Most of human evolutionary history unfolded in wild and messy natural settings, and we evolved to respond to such conditions. Modern societies, however, have become increasingly effective at creating cleaner and safer environments. Sanitation, antibiotics and other advances have greatly reduced infectious disease. Yet exposure to a diverse range of microorganisms also plays a role in the development of our microbiome and immune systems. Excessively sanitised environments may therefore remove some of the microbial diversity that our bodies need. Something similar may happen with psychological wellbeing. Modern environments are designed to minimise risks and maximise comfort and convenience. At the same time, experiences of difficulty, uncertainty and failure provide opportunities to develop coping skills and resilience. By removing the chance to encounter such experiences, particularly during the formative years of childhood, people may become less capable of dealing with them when they inevitably occur. AI could accelerate hyperselection Artificial intelligence (AI) could intensify hyperselection because optimisation no longer needs to proceed at the speeds afforded by humans or previous technologies. Algorithms analyse the behaviour of millions of people and continuously learn which songs, videos, products or other content attract the most attention. Generative AI can then produce enormous quantities of new content based on patterns that have already proven successful. This creates a feedback loop. AI identifies what works, produces or recommends more of it, and uses the resulting information to optimise its outputs even further. Importantly, much of this process can occur without humans having to identify the successful formula themselves. As AI becomes integrated into more areas of life, hyperselection could therefore occur faster and across a much wider range of domains. Despite having access to an unprecedented volume of information and content, people may find that everything from entertainment and news to advice and creative work begins to look, sound and feel increasingly alike. What can we do about it? The lesson is not that optimisation is bad. Making things safer, cleaner and more efficient has produced enormous improvements in human life. Rather, we need to recognise that there can also be costs to optimising everything. One way to address this is to treat the preservation of adaptive variance as a design principle. For example, universities could make room for risky research rather than rewarding only predictable scientific output. Cities could preserve unique local businesses and spaces even when they are less commercially efficient. More generally, we can create more room for exploration and mastery, rather than treating every failure as something to be avoided. If we become too good at eliminating everything that does not work, we may also lose the very thing that makes life interesting, enriches our experiences, and provides the conditions for growth and flourishing.
